See the sections titled “1.1.5 Constraints on the critical inputs supporting compute could limit our ability to secure adequate compute.” and “1.1.44 Our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected by war, terrorism, natural disasters, public health crises, political crises, or other unexpected events.” 1.1.41 If we are unable to make acquisitions and investments, or successfully integrate them into our business, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. As part of our business strategy, we will continue to consider a wide array of potential strategic transactions, including acquisitions of businesses, new technologies, services, and other assets and strategic investments that complement our business. We have previously acquired and continue to evaluate targets that operate in relatively nascent markets, and there is no assurance that such acquired businesses will be successfully integrated into our business or generate substantial revenue. In addition, we may overpay for acquisition targets or make investments at valuations that do not ultimately prove justified by the targets’ performance, strategic value, or market conditions, which could adversely affect our financial condition. We may be unable to identify or complete prospective and attractive strategic transactions for many reasons, including competition from other potential acquirers, the effects of consolidation in our industry, and potentially high valuations of acquisition candidates. Even if we identify strategic transactions or enter into agreements with respect to such transactions, applicable antitrust laws and other regulations may limit our ability to acquire targets or force us to divest all or a portion of our business or an acquired business. If we are unable to identify suitable targets or complete acquisitions, our growth prospects may suffer, and we may not be able to realize sufficient scale and technological advantages to compete effectively. Acquisitions involve many risks, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations, including: • intense competition for suitable acquisition targets, which could increase prices and adversely affect our ability to consummate deals on favorable or acceptable terms; • failure or material delay in closing a transaction; • transaction-related lawsuits or claims; • difficulties in integrating the technologies, operations, existing contracts, and personnel of an acquired company; • difficulties in retaining key employees, business partners, or customers of an acquired company; • challenges with integrating the brand identity of an acquired company with our own; • diversion of financial and management resources from existing operations or alternative acquisition opportunities; • failure to realize the anticipated benefits or synergies of a transaction at all or within the expected timeframe;

 
53 • the incurrence of debt or dilution related to equity issuances in connection with a transaction; • failure to identify or address the problems, liabilities, or other shortcomings or challenges of an acquired company or technology, including issues related to copyrights and other intellectual property, regulatory compliance practices, litigation, revenue recognition, or other accounting practices, or employee or user issues; • risks that the acquired company could have a negative impact on our company culture; • risks that regulatory bodies may enact new laws or promulgate new regulations that are adverse to an acquired company or business; • risks that regulatory bodies do not approve our acquisitions or business combinations or delay such approvals; • theft of our trade secrets or confidential information that we share with potential acquisition candidates; • risk that an acquired company or investment in new services cannibalizes a portion of our existing business; and • adverse market reaction to an acquisition. If we fail to address the foregoing risks or other problems encountered in connection with past or future acquisitions of businesses, new technologies, services, and other assets, strategic investments, and other strategic transactions, or if we otherwise fail to realize the expected benefits of such acquisitions or investments, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. 1.1.42 Unfavorable media coverage regarding our business, our models, platform, and applications, the impacts of AI, and the AI industry more broadly could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. As our business has grown and as interest in us and the AI industry overall has increased, we have attracted, and may continue to attract, significant media coverage, public commentary, and scrutiny from time to time. This coverage and commentary have included, and we expect will continue to include, recurring narratives concerning the potential adverse societal impacts of AI, including that AI may displace or eliminate jobs, may be misused or otherwise cause harm, and may pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity. We have been, and may continue to be, a particular focus of such narratives, and unfavorable coverage of the AI industry generally may be attributed to us, in each case regardless of whether the underlying concerns are well-founded or specifically applicable to our models, platform, or applications. Unfavorable publicity regarding us, our partners, or the AI industry more broadly could adversely affect our reputation and brand, as described in the section titled “1.1.16 If we are unable to maintain and enhance our brand and reputation, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected.” Negative media coverage, including public figures making negative or threatening statements about our company, whether accurate or not, could also adversely affect our brand and reputation and may reduce market acceptance of our models, platform, and applications or impair our ability to attract and retain customers. As public awareness of our brand increases, any issues that draw media attention may have an amplified adverse effect on our reputation. If unfavorable media coverage or adverse public perceptions persist or intensify, the demand for our models, platform, and applications could decline and our brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. 1.1.43 We will incur increased costs and demands upon management as a result of complying with the laws and regulations affecting public companies, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. As a public company, we will incur greater legal, accounting, and other expenses than we incurred as a private company. For example, we are subject to the reporting requirements of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (“U.S. Exchange Act”), the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (“Sarbanes-Oxley Act”), the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, the rules and regulations of the SEC, and the listing standards of the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The U.S. Exchange Act requires, among other things, that we file annual, quarterly, and current reports with respect to our business and results of operations. Compliance with these requirements will increase our legal, accounting, and financial compliance costs, and increase demand on our systems, making some activities more time-consuming and costly. In addition, changing laws, regulations, and standards relating to reporting obligations and corporate governance disclosure are creating uncertainty for public companies, which could result in continued uncertainty regarding compliance matters and higher costs. We expect these rules and regulations to make it more expensive for us to obtain director and officer liability insurance, and we may be required to accept reduced policy limits

 
54 and coverage or incur substantially higher costs to maintain the same or similar coverage. As a result, it may be more difficult for us to attract and retain qualified individuals to serve on our board of directors or as our executive officers. As a public company, we expect to incur significant expenses and devote substantial management effort toward ensuring compliance with the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. In that regard, we will need to hire additional accounting and financial staff with appropriate public company experience and technical accounting knowledge. In addition, as a public company, we may be subject to stockholder activism, which can lead to substantial costs, distract management, and impact the manner in which we operate our business in ways we cannot currently anticipate. As a result of disclosure of information in this prospectus and in our public filings with the SEC as required of a public company, our business and financial condition will become more visible, which we believe may result in threatened or actual litigation, including by competitors and other third parties. If such claims are successful, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected, and even if the claims do not result in litigation or are resolved in our favor, these claims, and the time and resources necessary to resolve them, may divert the resources of our management and our board of directors, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Further, many members of our management team have limited experience managing a publicly traded company, interacting with public company investors, and complying with the increasingly complex laws and regulations pertaining to public companies. Our management team may not successfully or efficiently manage our transition to being a public company subject to significant regulatory oversight and reporting obligations under the federal securities laws and the continuous scrutiny of securities analysts and investors. These new obligations and constituents will require significant attention from our management and may divert their attention away from the day-to-day management of our business, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.1.44 Our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected by war, terrorism, natural disasters, public health crises, political crises, or other unexpected events. War, terrorist attacks, and other acts of political violence, or any significant natural disaster, such as an earthquake, fire, hurricane, tornado, flood, or significant power outage, may disrupt our operations, mobile networks, the internet, data centers, or the operations of our partners or third-party service providers, and the impact of climate change may increase these risks. In particular, our corporate headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area, a region known for seismic activity and increasingly for the threat of fires. In addition, any public health crises, pandemics, political crises, terrorist attacks, war and other political or social instability, other geopolitical developments, or other catastrophic events, whether in the United States or in non-U.S. geographies, may adversely affect our operations or macroeconomic conditions. For example, an act of terrorism, armed conflict, or escalation of geopolitical tensions could result in physical damage to or destruction of data centers and other critical infrastructure, whether owned or operated by us or our third- party providers, as well as disruptions to power, cooling, or network connectivity necessary to operate such facilities. The impact of any of the foregoing or other disruption to us, our partners, or other third parties may result in system interruptions and degradation, reputational harm, delays in our product development, lengthy interruptions in our services, data breaches, malware, and other security or hacking incidents, all of which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. All of the aforementioned risks may be further increased if our disaster recovery plans prove to be inadequate. Further, the insurance we maintain may be insufficient to cover our losses resulting from such business interruptions, and any incidents may result in loss of, or increased costs of, such insurance. 1.1.45 If we are unable to ensure that our models, platform, and applications interoperate with a variety of software applications that are developed by others, including our integration partners, we may become less competitive and our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected. Our models, platform, and applications must integrate with a variety of hardware and software platforms, and we need to continuously modify and enhance our models, platform, and applications to adapt to changes in hardware, software, and browser technologies. In particular, we have developed our models, platform, and applications to be able to easily integrate with third-party applications, including the applications of software providers that compete with us as well as our partners, through the interaction of APIs. In general, we rely on the providers of such software systems to allow us access to their APIs to enable these integrations. We are typically subject to standard terms and conditions of such providers, which govern the distribution, operation, and fees of such software systems, and which are subject to change by such providers from time to time. Our business will be harmed if any provider of such software systems: • discontinues or limits our access to its software or APIs;

 
55 • modifies its terms of service or other policies, including fees charged to, or other restrictions on, us or other software developers; • changes how information is accessed by us or our customers; • establishes more favorable relationships with one or more of our competitors; or • develops or otherwise favors its own competitive offerings over our models, platform, and applications. Further, we depend in part on operating systems, including mobile operating systems such as iOS and Android, and their respective application stores, such as Apple’s App Store and Google’s Play Store, to drive downloads of our Claude app. If such operating systems or application stores limit the availability of our app, make changes that degrade the functionality of our app, increase the cost of using our app, impose terms of use unsatisfactory to us, or modify their search or ratings algorithms in ways that are detrimental to us, or if our competitors’ placement in such mobile operating systems’ application store is more prominent than the placement of our app, our user growth could be adversely affected. Any changes in such operating systems and application stores that degrade the functionality of our app or give preferential treatment to our competitors’ apps could adversely affect our platform’s usage across devices. Some marketplaces have explored changing their policies regarding what content is acceptable within an application. If we are unable to adapt to such changes, this could adversely affect our platform’s access to and usage within those ecosystems. As new mobile devices and mobile platforms are released, there is no guarantee that certain mobile devices will continue to support our platform or effectively roll out updates to our apps. Additionally, in order to deliver a high- quality app, we need to ensure that our models, platform, and applications are designed to work effectively with a range of mobile technologies, systems, networks, and standards. We may not be successful in developing or maintaining relationships with key participants in the mobile industry that enhance users’ experience. If users encounter any difficulty accessing or using our apps on their mobile devices or if we are unable to adapt to changes in popular mobile operating systems, our prospects, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. Third-party models, platforms, and applications are constantly evolving, and we may not be able to modify our models, platform, and applications to assure their compatibility with those of other third parties. In addition, some of our competitors may be able to disrupt the operations or compatibility of our models, platform, and applications with their models, platforms, or applications, or exert strong business influence on our ability to, and the terms on which we, operate our models, platform, and applications. Should any of our competitors modify their products or standards in a manner that degrades the functionality of our models, platform, and applications or gives preferential treatment to competitive models, platforms, or applications, whether to enhance their competitive position or for any other reason, the interoperability of our models, platform, and applications with these products could decrease and our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. Further, if we are not permitted or able to integrate with these and other third-party applications in the future, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. 1.1.46 Many of the risks we face are interconnected and may compound or trigger cascading adverse effects across our business, which could amplify their overall impact. Our business and operations are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, as described in this section “1 Risk Factors,” many of which are interrelated, such that the occurrence of one risk event may exacerbate or trigger additional risk events, and the combined effect may be materially greater than the impact of any individual risk event in isolation. For example, unfavorable developments in intellectual property laws or adverse outcomes in copyright or other litigation could require us to modify, retrain, or limit the capabilities of our models, increasing costs and reducing the performance or competitiveness of our models, platform, and applications, which could in turn harm customer demand, revenue, and our reputation and brand. In addition, constraints on the availability or cost of compute could similarly limit our ability to develop and deploy advanced models, delay product launches, reduce service reliability, and adversely affect our revenue growth, while also affecting customer trust and perception of our offerings. If our revenue growth is limited and we do not have sufficient additional sources of capital, we may be unable to acquire necessary compute or invest in our talent to remain at the technological frontier or to support our customers, or we may face breaches of covenants or defaults under the A&R Credit Agreement and certain of our commercial agreements. If we were to breach covenants or default under the A&R Credit Agreement or certain of our commercial agreements, such an event could trigger cross-defaults, accelerate repayment obligations, restrict our access to capital, and further constrain our operations and growth, potentially magnifying other financial, operational, and reputational risks. Because these and other risks may interact in complex and unpredictable ways, particularly in a fast-moving industry characterized by technological change, evolving regulation, and emerging business models, we may not be able to foresee or effectively manage all potential consequences. If one risk triggers or intensifies others, or if multiple adverse events occur

 
56 concurrently or in close succession, our prospects, reputation, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. 1.2 Risks Related to Privacy, Cybersecurity, and Intellectual Property 1.2.1 The application of certain copyright law doctrines and contractual interpretations of open- source licenses to modern AI model training are uncertain. The application of certain copyright law doctrines and contractual interpretations of open-source licenses to modern AI model training have not been authoritatively resolved by U.S. and non-U.S. courts as of this date. We have a good faith belief that we own or possess all sufficient legal rights and/or defenses to the training data used in or with our AI models, platform, and applications, which is based in part on our belief that our use or acquisition of the training data used in or with our AI models, platform, and applications constitutes “fair use” of such training data under copyright law doctrine. In addition, copyright laws in some jurisdictions outside the United States generally do not recognize fair use, and our reliance on analogous exceptions is subject to evolving conditions and to adverse or unsettled judicial interpretation in those jurisdictions. If a court of law disagrees with our belief that our use or acquisition of such training data constitutes fair use or otherwise concludes that it violates copyright law, for example, by adopting the reasoning in Bartz (as defined below), including without limitation in currently active litigation against us or another company in our industry, our business may be adversely affected. In particular, adverse rulings in litigation involving other AI developers, regardless of the specific facts, data practices, or legal theories at issue in those cases, could establish legal precedents or interpretations of copyright law that apply broadly across the industry and limit our ability to train, develop, or deploy AI models, even if our own data procurement and usage practices differ. Such outcomes could restrict access to certain categories of training data, narrow the scope of available legal defenses, or impose new licensing, compliance, or operational requirements across the AI industry. For example, if we cannot rely on the fair use doctrine to access copyrighted work for training our models, we may be required to pay significant fees to obtain a license to such training data or our ability to further develop our models, platform, and applications and distribute models trained on such data at issue could be adversely affected. In addition, an adverse ruling against us or another company in our industry could result in injunctive relief that restricts our ability to use or distribute models trained on the data at issue or could require us to retrain affected models from scratch at substantial cost. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. 1.2.2 We are subject to complex and evolving laws, regulations, and other legal obligations related to privacy and data protection, and any actual or perceived failure to comply with such obligations could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We are subject to a range of laws and regulations in the EU, the United States, and other jurisdictions, and other legal obligations relating to privacy, data protection, and the collection, use, transfer, storage, and other processing of data. These laws, regulations, and other legal obligations vary across jurisdictions, and include comprehensive frameworks such as the General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (“GDPR”), laws that impose sector-specific obligations, and those that impose specific requirements or restrictions on the handling of particular types of data, such as personal data that is considered sensitive. These obligations are not harmonized, continue to evolve in scope, present technical and operational complexities and challenges, and may conflict or impose overlapping or inconsistent obligations. Further, these laws and regulations, as well as other laws and regulations not originally enacted to address privacy or data protection, continue to evolve as they are applied to new technologies, including AI, and may be interpreted or enforced in ways that are inconsistent, unclear, novel, or subject to significant regulatory discretion. Additionally, plaintiffs, class action counsel, state attorneys general, and other claimants continue to pursue claims against AI companies relating to data handling, privacy, and cybersecurity; similar disputes could arise against us and they could take the form of privacy, cybersecurity, breach of contract, tort, or other claims. New or evolving laws, regulations, regulatory interpretations, claims, and novel or inconsistent application of existing laws and regulations to us, or our evolving contractual or other legal obligations, including those that arise as we seek to enter into new markets or product offerings, may require us to modify our models, platform, and applications, policies, and practices, delay or limit the development or deployment of certain features, increase compliance and litigation costs, and result in fines or penalties. Our compliance obligations and expenditures, and our exposure thereunder, may vary depending on both how customers access and use our models, platform, and applications, including through our first-party offerings or third- party distribution channels, and on the nature of data processed in connection with those offerings. For example, our costs and regulatory exposure may vary based on the demands we receive from individuals, regulators, and other parties seeking to exercise rights under privacy or data protection laws. We may be subject to additional obligations, restrictions, or exposure in connection with the processing of data that is considered sensitive under applicable laws. In connection with the development, deployment, and improvement of our services, including model training,

 
57 improvement, and inference, we have faced, and may face in the future, operational errors or claims or assertions that our use or processing of data, such as personal, sensitive, or confidential data, is inconsistent with our obligations. Failure to secure data against risks to its confidentiality, integrity, or availability may result in legal obligations, such as notification obligations to individuals, regulators, or customers, which could result in additional legal and reputational risk. Any actual or perceived failure or inability by us, our personnel, or third parties acting on our behalf to comply with applicable privacy or data protection requirements, our contractual commitments, or our public statements regarding our data practices could result in investigations, litigation, fines, penalties, or other liability; require us to change our models, platform, and applications, policies, or practices; reduce customer demand or harm our reputation; require us to make public disclosures that could expose us to reputational and legal risks; and otherwise adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.2.3 We process personal and sensitive data for AI safety, and any actual or perceived failure to comply with the legal and regulatory obligations applicable to such processing could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Our commitment to AI safety requires us in some cases to access, collect, and process personal and sensitive data. While our approach and mechanisms relating to handling personal and sensitive data are designed to improve AI safety, they also subject us to compliance with evolving industry practices, laws and regulations, and increased risks related to the processing of sensitive data, such as increased risks of harm or litigation if we experience a security incident or unauthorized access to or processing of data. Further, laws and regulations not originally enacted to address AI safety are being applied to AI safety and may be increasingly interpreted or enforced in ways that are inconsistent, unclear, novel, or subject to significant regulatory discretion. Any actual or perceived failure to comply with AI safety requirements or our processing of personal or sensitive data for AI safety, or any actual or perceived security incident involving such data, could result in investigations, litigation, fines, penalties, or other liability; require us to change our policies or practices; reduce customer demand or harm our reputation; require us to make public disclosures that could expose us to reputational and legal risks; and otherwise adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.2.4 Any security breaches or other incidents, including those that affect our networks, systems, or data, or the networks, systems, or data of our service providers, suppliers, or customers, could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We store, handle, and otherwise process confidential, proprietary, and personal information, and our customers use our models, platform, and applications to process similarly sensitive information. We experience security risks, unintended exposure of or access to data, cyberattacks, and other attempts to gain unauthorized access to our information, sites, networks, systems, models, platform, and applications. These have resulted in, and may in the future result in, breaches of our security measures or those of our third-party service providers; unauthorized access to our sites, networks, systems, and accounts; unauthorized access to, and misappropriation of, personal, confidential, or proprietary information belonging to us, our customers, or others; viruses, worms, spyware, or other malware being served from our models, platform, and applications, networks, or systems; deletion or modification of content; the display of unauthorized content on our models, platform, and applications; interruption, disruption, or malfunction of operations; and other risks. We have in the past faced and in the future may face risks of phishing schemes and other cyberattacks, including by nation-states and state-sponsored actors, that continue to evolve in sophistication and volume, and may inherently be difficult to detect. Our proprietary model weights, corporate and financial data, and other core intellectual property represent particularly high-value targets for state-sponsored espionage and theft, and security researchers have identified companies at the frontier as priority targets for non-U.S. intelligence services3. The efforts of such state- sponsored actors to target us will likely increase over time, especially as we develop models with next-generation capabilities, and they may specifically target models which have not, or have not yet, been released to the general public. For example, state-sponsored actors may conduct cyberattacks specifically targeting Mythos in light of its advanced cyber vulnerability discovery capabilities. Our security capabilities continue to evolve, and certain aspects of our security program may not be sufficient to fully address the most sophisticated malicious actors, including well-resourced nation-state or state-sponsored groups, especially as those groups develop or obtain more powerful technology, which may include AI technology with offensive 3 Source: POLITICO, AI is now the weapon and the battlefield, August 3, 2026, discussing findings from CrowdStrike’s 2026 Threat Report.

 
58 capabilities similar to those displayed by Mythos. While we are actively investing in and enhancing our security infrastructure and controls, we have operated in the past, and may in the future operate, for periods of time with known limitations or gaps in our defenses as we continue to mature our security posture, and no information security program can be expected to prevent all possible incidents. There can be no assurance that we will be able to prevent or adequately detect and defend against all cyberattacks or other cybersecurity incidents affecting our systems, including incidents caused by nation-state and state-sponsored actors. An unauthorized exfiltration of our model weights could enable adversaries to bypass significant research investment, eliminate key competitive advantages, and potentially raise national security concerns if such technology is acquired by malicious actors. Further, if our model weights were obtained by unauthorized actors, such actors may be able to deploy such models outside of our usage policy, safety mechanisms, or monitoring frameworks, which could enable harmful or misuse scenarios that our safeguards are designed to prevent and could subject us to regulatory, reputational, or public scrutiny for having developed such capabilities. We have faced and expect to face insider threat risks and vulnerabilities related to hiring processes, identity verification, remote work environments, and compromised devices that could enable unauthorized access to sensitive systems or information. We have been and expect that we will continue to be targeted by individuals seeking employment under false identities, or with ulterior or malicious motives for seeking employment with us and the third parties on which we rely. We also face the risk that employees, contractors, or other personnel with authorized access to our systems, model weights, or other sensitive information may be compromised after joining us, including due to efforts by state-sponsored actors, competitors, or others to recruit, bribe, coerce, or otherwise induce such personnel, or to compromise their credentials or devices, in order to misappropriate sensitive information, enable unauthorized access, or introduce vulnerabilities into our systems, models, or products. Because personnel with authorized access to our model weights and other core intellectual property are particularly attractive targets, and because our remote and distributed work environment and our reliance on third-party vendors for certain key processes may limit our visibility into such conduct, we may be unable to prevent or timely detect these insider threats. In addition, in certain jurisdictions in which we operate or in which our vendors or the operators of facilities hosting our infrastructure are located, such personnel, vendors, or operators may be legally compelled to cooperate with government authorities, including intelligence and security agencies, in ways contrary to our interests, such as by providing access to our systems, data, or model weights. The laws of those jurisdictions may prohibit the affected parties from notifying us of such demands and may afford us limited or no ability to challenge them, and because such cooperation may be lawful where it occurs and involves personnel acting within their authorized access, our insider-threat and other security controls may not detect it. We have also seen, and expect to continue to see, industry-wide software supply chain vulnerabilities and attacks, which could affect our or third parties’ systems, or the security of our models, platform, and applications. Geopolitical tensions or armed conflicts around the world may increase these risks. As a result, we may be unable to prevent or timely detect all attempts to access or exfiltrate sensitive information, including by actors with substantial technical, financial, or geopolitical resources. As we continue to develop and deploy new features, including those incorporating AI, our systems are exposed to additional or evolving security risks, including those arising from emerging or imperfectly understood AI-specific threat vectors. Such AI-specific threats include prompt injection attacks that manipulate model behavior through malicious inputs, attempts to replicate or reverse engineer our proprietary models through systematic API queries, adversarial inputs designed to cause model failures or misclassifications, malicious corruption of training data that could compromise model integrity, and vulnerabilities in continuous integration and deployment pipelines that could allow insiders or other actors to inject malicious code that is subsequently propagated or amplified through AI-assisted development workflows. Such attacks may be difficult to detect, may not be addressed by traditional cybersecurity defenses, and may require specialized expertise, techniques, and infrastructure to mitigate. Further, features that rely on AI may be particularly susceptible to unanticipated vulnerabilities as both our understanding and the broader market’s understanding of AI-related security risks and mitigation techniques continue to develop. Our efforts to mitigate the foregoing risks may result in false positives and our mistakenly limiting or blocking certain users from accessing our technology, which could result in potential litigation or regulatory action. In addition, our agentic offerings interact with external tools, APIs, databases, code repositories, and other third-party systems, creating cybersecurity attack surfaces that are distinct from those applicable to traditional AI models. An adversary could manipulate the content of an external data source, API response, document, or web page processed by an agent to cause the agent to take harmful or unauthorized actions based on that manipulated input. An attacker could also attempt to compromise an active agent session and redirect the agent to perform malicious actions using the customer’s authenticated credentials and permissions. Because our agentic offerings are designed to take autonomous actions with real-world consequences, including executing code, modifying files, sending communications, and

 
59 completing transactions, a successful exploitation of these agentic attack surfaces could result in data exfiltration, unauthorized transactions, code injection, or other adverse effects, potentially across multiple customer deployments simultaneously. Traditional cybersecurity defenses, including firewalls, input validation, and access controls, may not be fully effective against these novel threat vectors, and the security community’s understanding of agentic-specific attack surfaces is still developing. We have in the past discovered, and may in the future discover, errors, vulnerabilities, or other defects, such as hallucinations (i.e., outputs in which an AI model generates factually incorrect or fabricated information with apparent confidence), in our models, platform, and applications only after deployment, including in connection with the development of new features, integrations, or capabilities. Such issues have resulted and may in the future result in service disruptions, degraded performance, unintended or harmful outputs, or the unauthorized disclosure of personal or proprietary information, including through security incidents that impact the networks, systems, and data of our customers. In addition, incidents impacting our customers may be caused by customer misconfiguration or misuse, or by inadequate access controls or other security practices by our customers. Such incidents, even if caused by customer misconfigurations or misuse, or by a customer’s lack of adequate security controls, may impact our reputation or the reputation of our models, platform, and applications, and may subject us to liability exposure, disruption of commercial relationships, or other damage. Cyberattacks, including cyberattacks directed at our networks, our customers’ networks, or the networks of third parties with which we have relationships, have been, and may in the future continue to be, amplified through the use of AI, including our models, platform, and applications. Such capabilities may be used to automate or scale attacks, impersonate employees or members of senior management, or otherwise gain unauthorized access to our systems or those of our customers, partners, or vendors. Failures in our internal systems or controls, security breaches, failures to comply with our privacy or data protection commitments, or other incidents, whether resulting from malicious activity, human error, or system limitations, could adversely affect our reputation, brand, and business and impair our ability to attract and retain customers. Our offices and the data centers that host our infrastructure, many of which are operated by third parties, are also exposed to physical threats as well as failures by the operators of those facilities. A physical intrusion could damage equipment, interrupt our services, or provide a path to our systems and data, including our model weights, that bypasses our network defenses. Although we have dedicated significant resources designed to identify and address these security risks, we cannot guarantee that our security measures will be effective or that our recovery protocols, backup, and other systems will be sufficient. Even where we detect an incident, our response may prove inadequate, including if we misjudge its severity, respond too slowly, or fail to fully remediate the underlying cause. In addition, incidents that appear minor when they occur may later prove significant when considered together with other incidents or with information learned afterward, and a series of related incidents, none of which is material on its own, could prove material in the aggregate. We continue to devote significant resources to protect against security breaches and other incidents, and we may need to devote significant resources in the future to mitigate and address problems caused by breaches and other incidents, which may divert resources from the growth and expansion of our business. Any actual or perceived security breach or other incident experienced by us or third parties with whom we do business, particularly our CSPs, could damage our reputation and brand, cause our business to suffer, require us to expend significant capital and other resources, cause us to incur increasing costs, including costs to deploy additional personnel and protection technologies, train employees, and engage third-party experts and consultants, expose us to litigation or regulatory action, cause us to violate applicable privacy, data protection, security, and other laws and regulations, subject us to adverse publicity and a loss of confidence in our security measures, and cause us to incur significant fines, penalties, and other liability exposure, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We have taken steps to limit our liability for certain incidents, for example through warranty disclaimers and limitations of liability in our terms of service, but those contractual protections may not be upheld, or may not apply to certain claims, or may otherwise be insufficient to limit our liability exposure under applicable law. In the EU, we face increasingly stringent regulatory reporting obligations for cybersecurity and AI-related incidents. Under the GDPR, we must notify the competent regulators about incidents that involve personal data and are likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals. Similarly, the EU Network and Information Security Directive 2022/2555 (“NIS2”) requires us to notify the competent authorities of any significant cybersecurity incident through a staged process. In addition, the EU AI Act requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep track of, document, and report serious incidents without undue delay to the AI Office established under the EU AI Act

 
60 and competent authorities. Going forward, providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems, as defined under the EU AI Act, will also have to report serious incidents or malfunctions without undue delay in certain circumstances. In the United States, companies are increasingly subject to analogous incident reporting obligations, including under federal and state data breach notification laws, such as the New York Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security (SHIELD) Act. In addition, certain U.S. states have adopted incident reporting laws specific to frontier model providers, such as the New York Responsible AI Safety and Education Act (RAISE Act) and the California Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act. These frameworks create heightened compliance and liability exposure in case of delayed, incomplete, or inaccurate incident disclosures. While we currently maintain insurance that may cover certain costs, liabilities, and other losses in connection with security breaches and other incidents, the insurance market for such losses is continuously evolving, and we may be unable to obtain coverage for certain cybersecurity-related or data-related liabilities on commercially reasonable terms, or at all, leaving us exposed to potentially significant uninsured losses. Furthermore, there can be no guarantee that the insurance coverage we do maintain will be adequate to compensate us for the potential losses, or that any insurance claims we submit will be covered, paid in a timely manner, or paid at all by our insurance carrier or carriers. 1.2.5 We employ automated data collection across the web and use other methods to collect data for training our AI models, and such activities may subject us to liability or limit our ability to use the collected data, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We collect and use various data sources to train our AI models, including publicly available information from the internet, datasets licensed or commissioned from third parties, and synthetic data generated by our own models. We use such data across the stages of model development, including pre-training and post-training. To collect publicly available information, we utilize web scraping or web crawling techniques, book scanning, and other methods. While we take steps designed to ensure that our activities comply with applicable law, applicable robots.txt notices, and relevant technical measures such as paywalls or logins, our efforts may not always be successful. Further, we may not be able to verify whether information collected using such techniques is protected under privacy, copyright, or other intellectual property laws in certain cases, and our use of any such protected information may subject us to additional liability for intellectual property infringement or privacy violations. More broadly, inadequate documentation of training data sources, provenance, or chain of custody could create legal exposure, complicate our ability to respond to regulatory inquiries or litigation discovery requests, or raise concerns during due diligence by investors, partners, or potential acquirers that could adversely affect our strategic transactions or business relationships. Our data collection activities have in the past resulted, are presently the subject of, and may in the future result in, litigation or other actions filed or instituted against us, alleging that our scraping, web crawling, and other techniques to collect data violate the law. For example, Reddit, Inc. has filed suit against us, captioned Reddit, Inc. v. Anthropic PBC, alleging we improperly accessed posts stored on Reddit, Inc.’s platform in violation of its legal rights. On July 3, 2025, we filed a notice of removal of the case to federal court. The case was remanded to state court on March 30, 2026. The lawsuit is currently pending, and we continue to defend ourselves against the allegations. The costs of defending against such litigation, regardless of merit, are considerable, and such litigation may divert management and key personnel’s attention and resources, which may seriously harm our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Claims of allegedly illegal scraping and web crawling techniques may be extremely broad, and it may not be possible for us to conduct our business in such a way as to avoid all such claims. We may be required to settle such litigation on terms that are unfavorable to us. For example, a settlement may require us to discontinue such allegedly illegal practices, preclude us from using certain scraping and web crawling techniques, and/or require us to develop alternative technology or practices. The development of alternative technology or practices would require significant effort and expense or may not be successful. Similarly, if any litigation to which we may be a party fails to settle and we go to trial, we may be subject to an unfavorable judgment which may not be reversible upon appeal. The terms of a judgment may require us to cease some or all of our operations or require the payment of substantial amounts. Any of these events could cause our business, financial condition, and results of operations to be adversely affected.

 
61 1.2.6 We collect, integrate, and analyze data via agreements from multiple sources, including data provided by our customers and users and data sourced from third parties under contractual arrangements, and such activities may subject us to liability or limit our ability to use the collected data, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. If we or the customers, users, or third parties from which we source data lack sufficient rights to collect, use, process, share, or analyze certain third-party data—including for training or improving analytical or AI models—we could be subject to legal claims, regulatory scrutiny, or contractual liability. Such claims could require us to limit functionality, segregate data, or retrain models, and could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. The costs of defending against such litigation, regardless of merit, are considerable, and such litigation may divert management and key personnel’s attention and resources, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Claims of misappropriation, misuse, infringement, privacy violations, or other violations of intellectual property or contractual rights, as well as other claims related to using particular data, may be extremely broad, and as such, it is likely we will face certain claims in the ordinary course of business. 1.2.7 We have been, are currently defending against, and may in the future be subject to, intellectual property rights claims by third parties, which are extremely costly to defend, may require us to pay significant damages, and may limit our ability to use certain technologies, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. There is considerable intellectual property development activity in our industry. Our competitors, as well as a number of other entities, including non-practicing entities and individuals, may own or claim to own intellectual property rights relating to our industry or our technology. As we face increasing competition and our public profile increases, the possibility of intellectual property rights claims against us may also increase. To train our models, we use material from many sources, some of which may include third-party copyrighted content or trademarks. Regardless of whether the material is copyrighted or the trademarks are registered, parties who own the rights to that content or those trademarks, or distribute that content, may attempt to sue us based on intellectual property infringement or other theories. We also face claims that outputs generated by our models infringe, or facilitate infringement of, third-party works. Lawsuits asserting such claims have been filed, are pending, and may be filed in the future in the United States and internationally. For example, in September 2025, we reached an agreement to settle a copyright infringement class action, captioned Bartz, et al. v. Anthropic PBC (“Bartz”), for $1.5 billion, which was approved by the district court in July 2026. As additional examples, various publishers have filed suit against us alleging copyright infringement of song lyrics and unlawful removal of copyright management information in the cases captioned Concord Music Group, Inc., et al. v. Anthropic PBC, Concord Music Group, Inc., et al. v. Anthropic PBC et al., BMG Rights Management (US) LLC v. Anthropic PBC, Round Hill Music LP, et al. v. Anthropic PBC, Sony Music Publishing (US) LLC v. Anthropic PBC et al., and others. Similarly, a third party alleges we accessed and reproduced posts stored on the third party’s platform in violation of its legal rights and has filed suit against us, captioned Reddit, Inc. v. Anthropic PBC. The possibility of statutory damages under some intellectual property legal frameworks creates additional risk for us. We are vigorously defending ourselves in these pending lawsuits and believe we have meritorious defenses, though these lawsuits address novel issues and areas of law that make the results uncertain. We also face patent infringement claims, which may seek substantial damages or injunctive relief limiting our ability to use certain technologies, and we expect such claims may increasingly be asserted as our public profile grows. Moreover, certain of our competitors hold substantially larger patent portfolios than we do, which they could assert against us and which may limit our ability to obtain effective cross-licenses or to counter such assertions with our own patent rights. The costs of defending against such litigation, regardless of merit, are considerable, and such litigation may divert management and key personnel’s attention and resources, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Claims of misappropriation, misuse, infringement, or other violations of intellectual property rights, as well as other claims related to using particular content, may be extremely broad, and as such, it is likely we will face certain claims in the ordinary course of business. We may be required to settle such litigation on terms that are unfavorable to us. For example, a settlement may require us to obtain a license to continue practices alleged to violate a third party’s rights, which may not be available on reasonable terms and may significantly increase our operating expenses. Such a license may not be available to us at all. As a result, we may be required to develop alternative technology or practices or discontinue such allegedly infringing practices. The development of alternative technology or practices would require significant effort and expense or may not be successful.

 
62 Similarly, if any litigation to which we may be a party fails to settle and we go to trial, we may be subject to an unfavorable judgment which may not be reversible upon appeal. The terms of a judgment may require us to cease some or all of our operations or require the payment of substantial amounts. Any of these events could cause our business, financial condition, and results of operations to be adversely affected. We also offer to indemnify our contract counterparties for certain third-party infringement claims against them, and such indemnification obligations may be excluded from contractual limitation of liability provisions that limit our exposure. In certain cases, our indemnification obligations may be broad or unlimited in scope, which could expose us to significant contingent liabilities, particularly given the unsettled nature of intellectual property law as applied to AI- generated outputs and the potential for claims to arise from a wide range of customer use cases that we cannot predict or control. For example, certain of our agreements require us to defend and indemnify the counterparty, without a cap on our liability, against third-party claims alleging that our models, or outputs generated by our models, infringe third- party intellectual property rights. In addition, as described in the section titled “1.1.14 We may be exposed to liability, litigation, and regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models, and our contractual protections and insurance may be insufficient, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.” certain of our agreements with external evaluators and testing vendors require us to defend and indemnify the evaluator, without a cap on our liability, against certain third-party claims, including claims of intellectual property infringement. Third-party infringement claims may require us to initiate or defend protracted and costly litigation on behalf of our customers and distribution partners, regardless of the merits of these claims. If any of these claims succeed, we may be forced to pay damages on behalf of our customers and distribution partners, may be required to modify our allegedly infringing models, platform, and applications to make them non-infringing, or may be required to obtain licenses under the infringed intellectual property rights. If we cannot obtain all necessary licenses on commercially reasonable terms or are unable to modify our models, platform, and applications or technology so that they are no longer infringing, our customers may be forced to stop using our models, platform, and applications, and our distribution partners may be forced to stop selling our models, platform, and applications. Even if we do not litigate these matters to a judgment, we may be required to settle such litigation on terms that are unfavorable to us. 1.2.8 If we fail to adequately protect our intellectual property rights, our competitive position may be impaired, and we may lose valuable assets, generate reduced revenue, and incur costly litigation to protect our rights, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Our success is dependent, in part, upon protecting our intellectual property rights and proprietary information. We rely and expect to continue to rely on a combination of trademark, copyright, patent, and trade secret protection laws, along with contractual restrictions, to protect our intellectual property rights and proprietary information. However, we cannot guarantee that the steps we take to protect our intellectual property rights and proprietary information will be sufficient, or that we will have adequate remedies for any such failure. In particular, current or former employees, contractors, or other insiders with access to our proprietary model weights, training data, algorithms, research insights, or other proprietary information could misappropriate such information, whether for personal gain, to benefit competitors, to harm our company, or for other purposes, and our confidentiality agreements and internal security controls may not be sufficient to prevent or detect such malfeasance. Further, third parties have in the past, and may in the future, knowingly or unknowingly infringe or circumvent our intellectual property rights, and we may not be able to prevent infringement without incurring substantial expense. Litigation brought to protect and enforce our intellectual property rights has been, and would be, costly, time- consuming, and distracting to management and key personnel, and could result in the impairment or loss of portions of our intellectual property rights. Further, our efforts to enforce our intellectual property rights may be met with defenses, counterclaims, and countersuits attacking the validity and enforceability of our intellectual property rights and may result in injunctive relief or monetary damages against us. If the protection of our intellectual property rights is inadequate to prevent use or misappropriation by third parties, the value of our brand and other intangible assets may be diminished and competitors may be able to more effectively mimic our models, platform, and applications and methods of operations. In addition, due to the significant amount of discovery required in connection with intellectual property litigation, our confidential information may be compromised by disclosure during litigation. Any of these events would have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Our future success and competitive position depend in part upon our ability to obtain or maintain certain intellectual property rights used in our models, platform, and applications. While we have issued patents and have patent applications pending, we may be unable to obtain patent protection for the technology covered in our patent applications. In addition, we cannot ensure that any of the patent applications will be granted or that the claims allowed on any issued patents will be sufficiently broad to protect our technology or models, platform, and applications and

 
63 provide us with competitive advantages. Further, any issued patents may be challenged, invalidated, or circumvented by third parties. Many patent applications in the United States may not be public for a period of time after they are filed, and since publication of discoveries in the scientific or patent literature tends to lag behind actual discoveries by several months, we cannot be certain that we will be the first creator of inventions covered by any patent application we make or that we will be the first to file patent applications on such inventions. Because some patent applications may not be public for a period of time, there is also a risk that we could adopt a technology without knowledge of a pending patent application, which technology would infringe a third-party patent once that patent is issued. We also rely on unpatented proprietary technology. It is possible that others will independently develop the same or similar technology or otherwise obtain access to our unpatented technology. To protect our trade secrets and other proprietary information, our policy requires employees, consultants, and independent contractors to enter into confidentiality agreements. We cannot guarantee that these agreements will provide sufficient protection for our trade secrets, know-how, or other proprietary information in the event of any unauthorized use, misappropriation, or disclosure of such trade secrets, know-how, or other proprietary information, or that the employee, consultant, or independent contractor will not breach their confidentiality agreements with us. If we are unable to maintain the proprietary nature of our technologies, our business could be adversely affected. We also rely on our trademarks, trade names, and brand names to distinguish our models, platform, and applications from the products of our competitors and have registered or applied to register many of these trademarks in the United States and certain countries outside the United States. However, occasionally third parties have registered and acquired, and may in the future register or acquire, common law rights in identical or similar marks for products or solutions that also address similar markets to our own and have tried to enforce such rights. As we rely in part on brand names and trademark protection to enforce our intellectual property rights, efforts by third parties to limit use of our brand names or trademarks and barriers to the registration of brand names and trademarks in various countries may restrict our ability to promote and maintain a cohesive brand throughout our key markets. There can also be no assurance that pending or future U.S. or non-U.S. trademark applications will be approved in a timely manner or at all, or that such registrations will effectively protect our brand names and trademarks. Additionally, third parties have opposed, and may in the future oppose, our trademark applications or otherwise challenge our use of the trademarks. In the event that our trademarks are successfully challenged, we could be forced to rebrand our models, platform, and applications, which would result in loss of brand recognition and would require us to devote resources to advertising and marketing new brands. Although we take measures to protect our property, if we are unable to prevent the theft of our intellectual property or its exploitation, the value of our investments may be undermined and our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected. 1.2.9 We incorporate open-source software in our models, platform, and applications, which may subject us to litigation or other requirements, each of which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. A portion of the technologies we use in our models, platform, and applications incorporates open-source software, and we may incorporate open-source software in our models, platform, and applications in the future. From time to time, companies that use third-party open-source software have faced claims challenging the use of such open-source software and their compliance with the terms of the applicable open-source license. We may be subject to suits by parties claiming ownership of what we believe to be open-source software or claiming non-compliance with the applicable open- source licensing terms. Some open-source licenses require end-users who distribute or make available across a network software that includes open-source software to make available all or part of such software (which may include valuable proprietary code), at no cost, or license such software under the terms of the particular open-source license. While we employ practices designed to help ensure our compliance with the licenses of third-party open-source software and protect our valuable proprietary source code, we may inadvertently use third-party open-source software in a manner that exposes us to claims of non-compliance with the applicable terms of such license, including claims for infringement of intellectual property rights or for breach of contract. These risks may be heightened by our use of our own AI tools, including Claude Code, in our software development processes, as AI-generated code could incorporate or reproduce open-source software such that the associated license obligations, including copyleft requirements to disclose or license proprietary source code, apply to us without our knowledge. Similar concerns regarding AI-generated code could also lead enterprise customers to limit their use of our products. Further, there is an increasing number of open-source software license types, almost none of which have been tested in a court of law, resulting in a dearth of judicial guidance regarding the proper legal interpretation of such license types. If a third party makes a claim against us alleging that we have not complied with the conditions of the applicable open-source license, we could incur significant legal expenses defending against such allegations, expend substantial time and resources to re-engineer some or all of our software,

 
64 and could be subject to significant damages, enjoined from the sale of our models, platform, and applications that contained the open-source software, and required to comply with the conditions of the open-source license, which may include the public release of certain portions of our proprietary source code, each of which may have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations. In addition to risks related to license requirements, use of open-source software can lead to greater risks than use of third-party commercial software because open-source licensors generally do not provide warranties or other contractual protections regarding misappropriation, misuse, infringement, ownership, misattribution, or other violations, the quality of the code, or the origin of the open-source software. Many of the risks associated with the use of open-source software cannot be eliminated and may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. For instance, open-source software is developed by programmers beyond our control and may have security vulnerabilities, defects, or errors of which we may not be aware. Even if we become aware of any such vulnerabilities, defects, or errors, it may take a significant amount of time for either us or the relevant programmers to address such vulnerabilities, defects, or errors. Such a delay may negatively impact our models, platform, and applications, including by adversely affecting the market’s perception of our models, platform, and applications, impairing the functionality of our models, platform, and applications, or delaying the launch of new features or functionality on our models, platform, and applications, any of which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.2.10 We currently, and may in the future, license technology from third parties for use in our models, platform, and applications, and our inability to maintain those licenses could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations, and our use of such third-party technology could subject us to litigation. We currently incorporate, and may in the future incorporate, technology that we license from third parties into our models, platform, and applications. If we are unable to obtain or continue to use or license these technologies on reasonable terms, or if these technologies become unreliable, unavailable, or fail to operate properly, we may not be able to secure adequate alternatives in a timely manner or at all, and our ability to offer our models, platform, and applications and remain competitive in our market would be harmed. Further, licensing technologies from third parties exposes us to increased risk of being the subject of intellectual property infringement claims and vulnerabilities due to, among other things, our lower level of visibility into the development process with respect to such technology and the care taken to safeguard against risks. We cannot be certain that our licensors do not or will not infringe on the intellectual property rights of third parties or that our licensors have or will have sufficient rights in the licensed technology or related intellectual property rights in all jurisdictions in which we may sell or offer our models, platform, and applications. Some of our agreements with our licensors may be terminated by them or otherwise provide for a limited term. If we are unable to continue to license technology because of intellectual property infringement claims brought by third parties against our licensors or against us, or if we are unable to continue our license agreements or enter into new licenses on commercially reasonable terms, our ability to develop and sell our models, platform, and applications containing or dependent on that technology would be limited, and our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. Additionally, if we are unable to license technology from third parties, we may be forced to acquire or develop alternative technology, which we may be unable to do in a commercially feasible manner, or at all, and may require us to use alternative technology of lower quality or performance standards. This could limit or delay our ability to offer new or competitive offerings and increase our costs. Third-party software we rely on may be updated infrequently, unsupported, or include errors or vulnerabilities that may not be resolved in a timely manner, any of which may result in errors in our own models, platform, and applications or expose our models, platform, and applications to vulnerabilities. Any impairment of the technologies or of our relationship with these third parties could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.2.11 Our development of solutions that replace or reduce reliance on third-party vendors may expose us to litigation and other disputes. We develop and deploy proprietary and partner-based solutions that replace, deprecate, or reduce our reliance on third- party vendors, including vendors that historically provided software, services, or infrastructure supporting our business. These vendors may perceive our actions as adversely affecting their business interests and may assert claims against us, including claims for breach of contract, intellectual property infringement (including patents, copyrights, or trade secrets), misuse of confidential or proprietary information, tortious interference, or unfair competition. Such claims may be asserted regardless of their merit and could result in costly litigation, settlements, injunctions, or restrictions on our ability to deploy or expand our models, platform, and applications. Defending against these claims

 
65 could divert management and key personnel’s attention and resources, require significant legal expenditures, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.2.12 We may be subject to claims that we or our employees have misappropriated the intellectual property of other companies, particularly as we hire employees from other AI and technology companies. Our success depends in part on our ability to attract and retain highly skilled employees, including engineers, data scientists, and researchers with experience in AI and machine learning. As competition for AI talent continues to intensify, we have hired and may in the future hire employees who previously worked for or have otherwise been involved with competitors or companies operating in related technology areas, and certain of our employees have left and others may leave to work for such competitors. These employees may have had access to proprietary or confidential information, including trade secrets, of their former employers. Although we require employees to comply with confidentiality and intellectual property obligations, we may nonetheless be subject to claims that we or our employees have misappropriated or improperly used trade secrets or other intellectual property of competitors or other companies. Such claims may be asserted even if we believe they are without merit and even in the absence of any intentional misconduct. Defending against these claims could be costly, time-consuming, and disruptive, and could divert management attention and resources away from our business. In addition, such disputes could result in damages, settlements, injunctive relief, restrictions on our ability to use certain technologies, limitations on the roles of certain employees, or reputational harm. Any of the foregoing could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 1.3 Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters 1.3.1 We are subject to claims, lawsuits, investigations, executive and administrative orders and directives, other regulatory actions, and various actions and proceedings, and face potential liability, expenses for legal claims, and harm to our business. We are subject to claims, lawsuits, arbitration proceedings, government inquiries and investigations, executive and administrative orders and directives, and other legal, regulatory, and administrative actions and proceedings, including those involving intellectual property disputes, compliance with regulatory requirements, government approvals and authorizations, labor and employment, anti-discrimination, commercial disputes, competition, privacy, consumer protection, customer complaints, advertising, and other matters relating to our technology, models, platform, and applications, and we may become subject to additional types of claims, lawsuits, arbitration proceedings, government inquiries and investigations, executive and administrative orders and directives, and other legal, regulatory, and administrative actions and proceedings as our business grows and as we deploy new technologies, models, platforms, and applications. In particular, as our models, platform, and applications increasingly include agentic AI systems capable of taking autonomous actions with real-world consequences, we may face novel legal theories of liability, including intellectual property infringement, product liability, agency, and negligence claims, that have not been tested in the context of autonomous AI systems and for which the scope of our potential exposure is uncertain. In addition, as we expand our healthcare and life sciences offerings, regulators may conclude that certain of our products, or our customers’ use of them, are subject to healthcare regulation or to other laws governing healthcare and health information, which could require us to obtain authorizations, modify or restrict our offerings, or incur significant compliance costs. Errors or other undesirable outputs from our models in these contexts could contribute to patient harm, compromised research, or regulatory failures by our customers, and could expose us to claims from customers, patients, and other third parties, as well as to regulatory inquiries and enforcement actions. We are also subject to antitrust and competition law risk arising from our public advocacy regarding AI safety and the responsible pace of AI development and from our participation in industry groups, safety collaborations, and standard- setting initiatives. Communications, advocacy, or collaboration among companies that develop frontier models, or conduct alleged to reflect coordination among such companies, may be characterized as concerted action subject to the antitrust and competition laws, including Section 1 of the Sherman Act and analogous state and non-U.S. laws, even where undertaken for safety purposes, conducted publicly, or intended as advocacy for governmental action or industry standards. In September 2026, a putative class action was filed against us and other developers of frontier models in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging that we and the other defendants agreed to restrain competition by slowing the pace at which we develop and improve our respective AI models, in purported violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act. The complaint seeks treble damages, injunctive relief, and other relief on behalf of a purported class of purchasers of the defendants’ paid consumer subscriptions. We disagree with the claims and intend to defend the matter vigorously, but the outcome of this and any similar proceeding is inherently uncertain.

 
66 Antitrust litigation can be complex, protracted, disruptive, and expensive, and an adverse outcome could result in treble damages and injunctive relief. We could also become subject to additional private litigation or to investigations or enforcement actions by the U.S. Department of Justice, the FTC, state attorneys general, or non-U.S. competition authorities. We have proposed public efforts to work with the U.S. government and other developers of frontier models to establish safety standards, including with respect to the pace of capability development, and have suggested that such collaboration may warrant a narrow exemption or safe harbor from antitrust laws. These proposals have drawn public opposition from political leaders, some of whom have characterized such efforts as anticompetitive regardless of the purpose of such exemption or safe harbor. There is no assurance that any such exemption or safe harbor will be adopted. Our advocacy for such an exemption, and any safety commitments we pursue with other developers of frontier models in its absence, could subject us to additional regulatory, litigation, and other risks.
