Our 2026 Plan was adopted by our board of directors on September 1, 2026, and approved by our stockholders on October 22, 2026. Our 2026 Plan will become effective as of the day immediately prior to the day the registration statement with respect to the U.S. offering becomes effective. Share Reserve. The maximum aggregate number of shares that may be issued under our 2026 Plan is: (i) 1,920,580,692 shares of our Class A common stock; plus (ii) the number of shares of our Class A common stock equal to the total shares of Class A common stock available for issuance pursuant to our 2021 Plan immediately prior to the termination of our 2021 Plan on the effective date of our 2026 Plan; plus (iii) the number of shares of our Class A common stock equal to the total shares of Class A common stock subject to awards previously granted under our 2021 Plan that, after the effective date of our 2026 Plan, would have returned to our 2021 Plan and become available for issuance pursuant to future awards under our 2021 Plan had our 2021 Plan not terminated on the effective date of our 2026 Plan. In addition, the number of shares that may be issued under our 2026 Plan will be increased on the first day of each fiscal year beginning with our 2027 fiscal year and ending on (and including) the first day of our 2036 fiscal year, in an amount equal to the lesser of: (i) 5% of the total number of shares of our common stock (including only all classes of common stock issued by the company that carry economic rights) outstanding on the last day of the calendar month prior to the date of such automatic increase (calculated on an as-converted basis); and (ii) such number of shares determined by our board of directors. To the extent an award should expire or be forfeited or become unexercisable for any reason without having been exercised in full, or is surrendered pursuant to an exchange program, the unissued shares that were subject thereto shall

 
247 continue to be available under our 2026 Plan for issuance pursuant to future awards. In addition, any shares which are retained by us to satisfy exercise or purchase price or any withholding taxes shall be treated as not issued and shall continue to be available under our 2026 Plan for issuance pursuant to future awards. Shares issued under our 2026 Plan and later forfeited to us due to the failure to vest or repurchased by us at a price no greater than the original purchase price paid to us for the shares shall again be available for future grant under our 2026 Plan. To the extent an award under our 2026 Plan is paid out in cash rather than shares, such cash payment will not reduce the number of shares available for issuance under our 2026 Plan. Plan Administration. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our 2026 Plan to our compensation committee. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator has the power to determine the terms of awards, including the recipients, the exercise price, if any, the number of shares subject to each award, the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock, the vesting schedule applicable to the awards, together with any vesting acceleration, the form of consideration, if any, payable upon exercise of the award and the terms of the award agreement for use under our 2026 Plan. The administrator also has the authority, subject to the terms of our 2026 Plan, to amend existing awards, to prescribe rules and to construe and interpret our 2026 Plan and awards granted thereunder and to institute an exchange program by which outstanding awards are amended to provide for a lower exercise price or surrendered or cancelled in exchange for awards with a lower exercise price, a different type of award under our 2026 Plan or a different equity incentive plan, cash, or a combination thereof. Eligibility. Employees, members of our board of directors who are not employees, and consultants (including, without limitation, employees of a staffing agency, professional employer organization, employer of record, and similar workers) are eligible to participate in our 2026 Plan. Types of Awards. Our 2026 Plan provides for the grant of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, RSUs, and stock bonus awards to our employees, directors, and consultants and the employees and consultants of our subsidiaries. Stock Options. The administrator may grant incentive stock options (within the meaning of Section 422 of the U.S. Code) and/or nonstatutory stock options under our 2026 Plan, provided that incentive stock options may only be granted to our employees and the employees of our subsidiaries. The exercise price applicable to such options must generally be equal to at least the fair market value of our Class A common stock on the date of grant. The term of an incentive stock option may not exceed 10 years; provided, however, that an incentive stock option held by a participant who owns more than 10% of the total combined voting power of all classes of our stock, or of certain of our subsidiary corporations, may not have a term in excess of five years and must have an exercise price equal to at least 110% of the fair market value of our Class A common stock on the grant date. The administrator will determine the methods of payment of the exercise price applicable to an option, which may include cash, shares, or other property acceptable to the administrator. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator determines the remaining terms of the options. Such terms may include, among other things, vesting upon the achievement of specific performance goals determined by the administrator and/or continued service. After the termination of service, the participant may exercise their option, to the extent vested, for the period of time stated in their option agreement. Except in the event of a termination for cause, options generally remain outstanding to the extent exercisable for the full term of the options. In no event may an option be exercised later than the expiration of its term. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement. Stock Appreciation Rights. Stock appreciation rights may be granted under our 2026 Plan. Stock appreciation rights allow the recipient to receive the appreciation in the fair market value of our Class A common stock between the date of grant and the exercise date. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator determines the terms of stock appreciation rights, including when such rights vest and become exercisable and whether to settle such awards in cash or with shares of our Class A common stock, or a combination thereof, except that the per share exercise price for the shares to be issued pursuant to the exercise of a stock appreciation right will be no less than 100% of the fair market value per share on the date of grant. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement. Restricted Stock. Restricted stock may be granted under our 2026 Plan. RSAs are grants of shares of our Class A common stock that are subject to various restrictions, including restrictions on transferability and forfeiture provisions. Shares of restricted stock will vest and the restrictions on such shares will lapse, in accordance with terms and conditions established by the administrator. Such terms may include, among other things, vesting upon the achievement of specific performance goals determined by the administrator and/or continued service. The administrator, in its sole discretion, may accelerate the time at which any restrictions will lapse or be removed. Recipients of RSAs generally will have voting

 
248 and dividend rights with respect to such shares upon grant without regard to vesting, unless the administrator provides otherwise. Shares of restricted stock that do not vest for any reason will be subject to our right of repurchase or forfeited by the recipient. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement. Restricted Stock Units. RSUs may be granted under our 2026 Plan and may include the right to dividend equivalents, as determined in the discretion of the administrator. Each RSU granted is a bookkeeping entry representing an amount equal to the fair market value of one share of our Class A common stock. The administrator determines the terms and conditions of RSUs, including the vesting criteria, which may include achievement of specified performance criteria and/or continued service. The administrator, in its sole discretion, may accelerate the time at which any restrictions will lapse or be removed. The administrator determines, in its sole discretion, the timing of payment and whether an award will be settled in stock, cash, or a combination thereof. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement. Stock Bonus Awards. Stock bonus awards may be granted under our 2026 Plan. The administrator may grant stock bonus awards in such amounts, and subject to such terms, as the administrator, in its sole discretion, will determine. A stock bonus award is an award of shares of our Class A common stock without a purchase price. All stock bonus awards may be made, but are not required to be made, pursuant to an award agreement. Payment of a stock bonus award may be made in the form of cash, shares, or a combination thereof, based on the fair market value of the shares subject to the stock bonus award on the date of payment, as determined in the sole discretion of the administrator. Outside Director Limitations. Stock awards granted during a single fiscal year under our 2026 Plan or otherwise, taken together with any cash fees paid during such fiscal year for services on our board of directors, shall not exceed $1,000,000 in total value for any non-employee director, except with respect to the first year of service in which case any stock awards granted and cash fees paid will not exceed $2,000,000 in total value (calculating the value of any such stock awards, in each case, based on the grant-date fair value of such stock awards for financial reporting purposes). Such applicable limit includes the value of any stock awards that are granted in lieu of all or a portion of any annual committee cash retainers or other similar cash-based payments. Stock awards granted to an individual while they were serving in the capacity as an employee or while they were an independent contractor but not a non-employee director will not count for purposes of the limitations described above. Non-Transferability of Awards. Unless the administrator provides otherwise, our 2026 Plan generally does not allow for the transfer of awards other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and only the recipient of an option or stock appreciation right may exercise such an award during their lifetime. Certain Adjustments. In the event of a stock split, reverse stock split, stock dividend, combination, consolidation, recapitalization (including a recapitalization through a large nonrecurring cash dividend or distribution of property, including shares of a subsidiary), or reclassification of the shares, subdivision of the shares, a rights offering, a reorganization, merger, spin-off, split-up, repurchase, or exchange of common stock or other securities of the company or other significant corporate transaction, or other change affecting the common stock, the administrator, in order to prevent dilution, diminution, or enlargement of the benefits or potential benefits intended to be made available under our 2026 Plan, will, in such manner as it may deem equitable, adjust the number, kind, and class of securities that may be delivered under our 2026 Plan and/or the number, class, kind, and price of securities covered by each outstanding award, and the terms and conditions of any outstanding award (including, without limitation, any applicable performance targets or criteria with respect thereto). Dissolution or Liquidation. In the event of a proposed winding up, dissolution, or liquidation of the company, the administrator will notify participants as soon as practicable prior to the effective date of such proposed transaction and all awards will terminate immediately prior to the consummation of such proposed transaction, to the extent not previously exercised or settled. Corporate Transaction. Our 2026 Plan provides that, in the event of certain significant corporate transactions, including: (1) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets; (2) a merger, consolidation, or other capital reorganization or business combination transaction of the company with or into another corporation, entity, or person; or (3) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any person becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of the company’s then-outstanding capital stock, each outstanding award will be treated as the administrator determines. Such determination, without the consent of any participant, may provide that such awards will be (i) continued if we are the surviving corporation; (ii) assumed by the surviving corporation or its parent; (iii) substituted by the surviving corporation or its parent for a new award; (iv) cancelled in exchange for a payment equal to the excess of the fair market value of our shares subject to such award over the exercise price or purchase price paid for such shares; (v) subject to full or partial acceleration of vesting, settlement, payment,

 
249 and/or expiration as of immediately prior to the corporate transaction; (vi) subject to full or partial lapse of forfeiture, repurchase, or reacquisition rights with respect to shares previously acquired pursuant to any awards as of immediately prior to the corporate transaction; (vii) in the case of outstanding options and/or stock appreciation rights, allowed to be exercised prior to the occurrence of the corporate transaction and terminated (for no consideration) upon the consummation of such corporate transaction if not exercised prior thereto; or (viii) cancelled in exchange for no consideration. Change in Control. The administrator may provide, in an individual award agreement or in any other written agreement between a participant and us, that the stock award will be subject to additional acceleration of vesting, settlement, payment, and/or expiration in the event of a change in control. Under our 2026 Plan, a “change in control” is generally (1) a merger, consolidation, or any other corporate reorganization in which the shares of capital stock of the company immediately before the transaction cease to represent immediately after such transaction at least a majority of the voting power of the continuing or surviving entity in substantially the same proportions immediately after such transaction as in effect before such transaction; (2) with certain limited exceptions, the consummation of the sale, transfer, or other disposition of all or substantially all of our assets; (3) a change in the effective control of the company which occurs on the date that a majority of our board members are replaced during any 12-month period by directors whose appointment or election is not endorsed by a majority of the members of our board of directors prior to the date of the appointment or election; or (4) the consummation of any transaction as a result of which any person or company becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of at least 50% of the total voting power represented by our then-outstanding voting securities. No transaction shall constitute a change in control (i) as the result of the initial effectiveness of the company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the effectiveness of the registration statement with respect to the U.S. offering, (ii) pursuant to clause (3) above until after the time at which both the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time have occurred, as such terms are defined in the company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the effectiveness of the registration statement with respect to the U.S. offering, (iii) if its primary purpose is to change the jurisdiction of the company’s incorporation or to create a holding company owned in substantially the same proportions by the persons who held company securities immediately before such transactions, or (iv) if required for compliance with Section 409A of the U.S. Code, a transaction will not be a change in control unless it is also a “change in the ownership or effective control of” the company or “a change in the ownership of a substantial portion of the assets of” the company as determined under applicable Treasury regulations. Compensation Recovery Policy. Awards granted under our 2026 Plan will be subject to reduction, cancellation, forfeiture, and/or recoupment in accordance with any compensation recovery policy as may be in effect as of the date of grant of such award, or as such policy is amended or another policy is adopted to comply with applicable laws. In addition, the administrator may impose such other compensation recovery or recoupment provisions in any award agreement as it determines necessary or appropriate. Amendment or Termination. Our administrator has the authority to amend, alter, suspend, or terminate our 2026 Plan, provided such action does not materially impair the existing rights of any participant unless otherwise provided in our 2026 Plan or mutually agreed otherwise. Our 2026 Plan will continue in effect until terminated by the administrator, but no options that qualify as incentive stock options may be granted after 10 years from the earlier of the board or stockholder approval of our 2026 Plan. We will obtain stockholder approval of any amendment to our 2026 Plan as required by applicable law or listing requirements. 9.12.2.18.2 Amended & Restated 2021 Stock Plan General. Our board of directors adopted our 2021 Plan on January 28, 2021 and last amended our 2021 Plan effective as of May 28, 2026. Our 2021 Plan will be terminated effective as of the day immediately prior to the day the registration statement with respect to the U.S. offering becomes effective, and no new awards will be granted under our 2021 Plan following the global offering, but previously granted awards will continue to be subject to the terms and conditions of our 2021 Plan and the award agreements evidencing such awards. Share Reserve. We have reserved for issuance pursuant to our 2021 Plan an aggregate of 3,864,826,090 shares of our Class A common stock. In general, if an award granted under our 2021 Plan (i) expires or is terminated, cancelled, or otherwise forfeited by a participant, (ii) a share subject to an award is withheld in satisfaction of the exercise price and/or tax withholding due in connection with such award, or (iii) a share previously issued pursuant to an award is forfeited or repurchased at the original purchase price paid for the share, then the number of unissued shares subject to any such award, and any such withheld, forfeited, or repurchased shares, will again become available for awards under

 
250 our 2021 Plan. Following the effectiveness of our 2026 Plan, such shares will again become available for awards under our 2026 Plan. Plan Administration. Our board of directors has administered our 2021 Plan before the global offering. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our 2021 Plan to our compensation committee following the global offering. Types of Awards. Our 2021 Plan provides for incentive and non-statutory stock options to purchase shares of our Class A common stock, RSAs, and RSUs. As of the date of this prospectus, we have issued stock options, restricted stock, and RSUs pursuant to our 2021 Plan. Non-transferability of Awards. Unless the administrator provides otherwise, our 2021 Plan generally does not allow for the transfer of awards other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and only the recipient of an option right may exercise such an award during their lifetime. Certain Adjustments. In the event of certain corporate events or changes in our capitalization, to prevent diminution or enlargement of the benefits or potential benefits available under our 2021 Plan, the administrator will make adjustments to one or more of the number, kind, and class of securities that may be delivered under our 2021 Plan and/or the number, kind, class, and price of securities covered by each outstanding award. Corporate Transaction. Our 2021 Plan provides that in the event of (i) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets, (ii) a merger, consolidation, or other capital reorganization or business combination transaction of us with or into another corporation, entity, or person, or (iii) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any “person” becomes the “beneficial owner,” directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of our then-outstanding capital stock (each, a “Corporate Transaction”), the administrator may, in its sole and absolute discretion and without the need for the consent of any participant, take one or more of the following actions contingent upon the occurrence of that Corporate Transaction with respect to outstanding awards granted under our 2021 Plan which provide for: (A) the continuation of such awards by us (if we are the surviving corporation); (B) the assumption of such awards by the surviving corporation or its parent; (C) the substitution by the surviving corporation or its parent of new options or equity awards for such awards; (D) the cancellation of such awards in exchange for a payment to the participants equal to the excess of (1) the fair market value of the shares or units subject to such awards as of the closing date of such Corporate Transaction over (2) the exercise price or purchase price paid or to be paid for the shares or units representing shares subject to the awards, as applicable; or (E) the cancellation of any outstanding awards or an outstanding right to purchase restricted stock, in either case, for no consideration. Amendment or Termination. Our board of directors may amend or terminate our 2021 Plan at any time. If our board of directors amends our 2021 Plan, we will ask our stockholders to approve the amendment if such approval is necessary or desirable to comply with applicable law. No further awards will be made under our 2021 Plan after the global offering. 9.12.2.18.3 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan General. Our ESPP was adopted by our board of directors on September 1, 2026, and approved by our stockholders on October 22, 2026. Our ESPP will become effective as of the day immediately prior to the day the registration statement with respect to the U.S. offering becomes effective. Our ESPP includes two components: a 423 component and a non-423 component. We intend the 423 component to qualify as an “employee stock purchase plan” within the meaning of Section 423 of the U.S. Code. The non-423 component authorizes grants of purchase rights that do not comply with Section 423 of the U.S. Code. Share Reserve. The maximum aggregate number of shares that may be issued under our ESPP is 128,038,713 shares of our Class A common stock. In addition, the number of shares that may be issued under our ESPP will be increased on the first day of each fiscal year beginning with our 2027 fiscal year and ending on (and including) the first day of our 2036 fiscal year, in an amount equal to the lesser of: (i) 1% of the total number of shares of our common stock (including only all classes of common stock issued by the company that carry economic rights) outstanding on the last day of the calendar month prior to the date of such automatic increase (calculated on an as-converted basis); and (ii) such number of shares determined by our board of directors. Plan Administration. Our ESPP is administered by our board of directors or a committee designated by our board of directors. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our ESPP to our compensation committee.

 
251 Eligibility. Generally, all regular employees, including executive officers, employed by us or by any of our designated affiliates and specified service providers (including non-U.S. service providers) or our designated affiliates may participate in our ESPP. Employees may have to satisfy one or more of the following service requirements before participating in the 423 components of our ESPP, as determined by the administrator, including: (1) continuous service with us or one of our affiliates for at least two years (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (2) being customarily employed for more than 20 hours per week (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (3) being customarily employed for more than five months per calendar year (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (4) is not a highly compensated employee within the meaning of Section 423(b)(4)(D) of the U.S. Code, or (5) such other criteria as our board of directors may determine to be consistent with Section 423 of the U.S. Code. No employee may purchase shares under the 423 component of our ESPP at a rate in excess of $25,000 worth of our Class A common stock based on the fair market value per share of our Class A common stock at the beginning of an offering for each year such a purchase right is outstanding. Finally, no employee will be eligible for the grant of any purchase rights under the 423 component of our ESPP if immediately after such rights are granted, such employee has voting power over 5% or more of our outstanding capital stock measured by vote or value under Section 424(d) of the U.S. Code. Offerings. Our ESPP is implemented through offerings pursuant to which participants are granted rights to purchase shares of our Class A common stock on specified dates during such offerings. Under our ESPP, we may specify offerings with durations of not more than 27 months and may specify shorter purchase periods within each offering. Each offering will have one or more purchase dates on which shares of our Class A common stock will be purchased by participants in the offering. An offering under our ESPP may be terminated under certain circumstances. The administrator will have the discretion to structure an offering so that if the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the first trading day of a new purchase period within that offering is less than or equal to the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the offering date for that offering, then that offering will terminate immediately as of that first trading day, and the participants in such terminated offering will be automatically enrolled in a new offering beginning on the first trading day of such new offering. Payroll Deductions. Participants who are employees may generally make contributions through payroll deductions (unless otherwise required by law or provided for in an offering). In the case of an offering under the 423 component, such percentage or maximum dollar amount of contributions may not exceed 15% of their earnings for the applicable offering. Contributions pursuant to the non-423 component will generally be made on an after-tax basis in a manner determined by the administrator. Shares of our Class A common stock will be purchased for the accounts of participants in our ESPP at a price per share that is not less than the lesser of (1) 85% of the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the first date of an offering, or (2) 85% of the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the date of purchase. Certain Adjustments. In the event of any change that is made in, or other events that occur with respect to, our Class A common stock subject to our ESPP or subject to any purchase right without the receipt of consideration by the company through merger, consolidation, reorganization, recapitalization, reincorporation, stock dividend, dividend in property other than cash, large nonrecurring cash dividend, stock split, liquidating dividend, combination of shares, exchange of shares, change in corporate structure, or other similar equity restructuring transaction, our board of directors will make appropriate and proportionate adjustments to: (1) the class(es) and maximum number of shares reserved under our ESPP, (2) the class(es) and maximum number of shares by which the share reserve may increase automatically each year, (3) the class(es) and number of shares subject to, and purchase price applicable to, all outstanding offerings and purchase rights, and (4) the class(es) and number of shares that are subject to purchase limits under ongoing offerings. Dissolution or Liquidation. In the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the company, any offering then in progress will be shortened by setting a new purchase date prior to the consummation of such proposed dissolution or liquidation. Our board of directors will notify each participant that the purchase date has been changed and that the participant’s purchase right will be exercised automatically on the new purchase date unless prior to such date the participant has withdrawn from the offering. Corporate Transactions. Our ESPP provides that in the event of certain significant corporate transactions, including: (1) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets; (2) a merger, consolidation, or other capital, reorganization or business combination transaction of the company with or into another corporation, entity, or person; or (3) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any person becomes the beneficial owner,

 
252 directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of our then-outstanding capital stock, a successor corporation may assume, continue, or substitute each outstanding purchase right. If the successor corporation does not assume, continue, or substitute the purchase right, the participants’ accumulated contributions will be used to purchase shares prior to the corporate transaction and the purchase rights will terminate immediately after such purchase. The administrator will notify each participant that the purchase date has been changed and that the participant’s purchase right will be exercised automatically on the new purchase date unless prior to such date the participant has withdrawn from the offering. Spin-Off. In the event of a spin-off or similar transaction, our board of directors may take actions deemed necessary or appropriate in connection with any ongoing offering, subject to compliance with applicable laws. In the absence of any such action, if an entity ceases to qualify as a related company under our ESPP, any participant in an ongoing offering employed by, or providing services to, such entity will be treated in the same manner as if the participant had terminated employment or service. Amendment or Termination. Our board of directors has the authority to amend, suspend, or terminate our ESPP at any time, except that, subject to certain exceptions described in our ESPP, no such action may materially impair outstanding rights under our ESPP. We will obtain stockholder approval of any amendment to our ESPP as required by applicable law or listing requirements. 9.12.3 Accruals for Pension Liabilities As of December 31, 2025, the total amount accrued by us for employer matching contributions under our 401(k) retirement plan for the members of our board of directors was approximately $17,000. 9.13 Shareholdings and Stock Options of Our Directors and Executive Officers Beneficial ownership of our shares of common stock of the members of our board of directors and executive officers, including through option rights, is set forth in section “11.1 Principal Stockholders.” 9.14 Certain Information Regarding our Directors and Executive Officers In the previous five years, no director or executive officer has been (i) convicted in relation to fraudulent offences, (ii) involved in any bankruptcies, receiverships, liquidations or companies put into administration, (iii) involved in any official public incrimination and/or sanctions by statutory or regulatory authorities (including designated professional bodies), and (iv) has ever been disqualified by a court from acting as a member of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies of an issuer or from acting in the management or conduct of the affairs of any issuer in the previous five years.

259 11.1.2 Major Shareholders, Voting Rights and Control Arrangements The following persons or entities have an interest in the Company’s capital or voting rights which is equal to or above 5% of capital or total voting rights: The LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors, through a special class of common stock, the Class T common stock. As of the date of this prospectus, the Company does not otherwise have any shareholder holding 5% or more of the voting rights in the Company. Immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, we will also issue a single share of Class F common stock, a special class of our common stock, to the Founder LLC. The Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T directors. Amazon and Google will hold 1,920,511,218 and 1,654,463,134 shares of our Class N common stock, respectively, immediately prior to the completion of the global offering and the concurrent private placement (after giving effect to the Preferred Stock Conversion and the Convertible Notes Conversion), and will hold 1,920,511,218 and 1,789,598,269 shares of our Class N common stock, respectively, immediately following the global offering and the concurrent private placement. The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a wholly owned subsidiary dedicated to our Company Purpose, will hold 7.1% of our outstanding capital stock. Immediately following the completion of the global offering and the concurrent private placement, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will hold 6.5% of our outstanding capital stock, subject to the assumptions set forth in the section titled “11.1.1 Notifiable Beneficial Ownership Under SEC Rules.” Amazon, Google and the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will only hold shares of Class N common stock, which is not entitled to vote on any matter that is submitted to a vote of stockholders except as otherwise required by law. Under our governance structure, we expect that the LTBT and the Founder LLC will collectively have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors, and the Founder LLC will have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future. Accordingly, holders of our Class A common stock generally will not be able to affect the outcome of any matter submitted to a vote of our stockholders or the election of our directors, regardless of how they vote. For further information on the voting rights attached to our shares of common stock, see “11.2.1.3 Our Capital Stock Following Completion of the Global Offering” and for additional information on the election and removal of our directors, see “9.4 Board of Directors.” We are considered a “controlled company” under the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements because the LTBT, as the sole holder of our Class T common stock, generally has the power to elect a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. Under Delaware law, a controlling stockholder of a public benefit corporation generally owes fiduciary duties when exercising control over the corporation, including the duty of loyalty when obtaining a non-ratable benefit at the expense of the corporation or its minority stockholders. The Delaware public benefit corporation provisions impose the statutory balancing requirement on the board of directors, which must manage the corporation in a manner that balances (i) the pecuniary interests of the stockholders, (ii) the best interests of those materially affected by the corporation’s conduct, and (iii) the specific public benefit or public benefits identified in the corporation’s certificate of incorporation. The Delaware courts have not yet addressed the role of controlling stockholder obligations in light of this balancing requirement. The LTBT’s purpose, however, mirrors the directors’ balancing obligations. Our governance structure is likely to have the effect of limiting the likelihood of an unsolicited merger proposal, unsolicited tender offer, or proxy contest for the removal of directors. See the section titled “1.5 Risks Related to our Governance Structure,” in particular sections “1.5.9 Provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws could make a merger, tender offer, proxy contest, or other significant corporate transaction difficult, potentially depressing the market price of our Class A common stock.” as well as “1.5.1 Our capital stock structure features certain provisions that are novel or otherwise not common among other corporations with multiple-class structures, and may effectively eliminate the ability of holders of our Class A common stock to influence important decisions, including a change in control.” and “1.5.2 Our capital structure will concentrate voting power with the Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT) and the Founder LLC for the foreseeable future and will result in the LTBT and the Founder LLC having voting power that is not derived from or proportionate to economic interests in the Company.” See also the sections titled “4.1.1.1 Public Benefit Corporation,” and “11.2 Description of Capital Stock.”

 
260 11.2 Description of Capital Stock Prospective investors should note that in connection with the global offering, we will reorganize our capital stock. For a description of our capital stock as it will be authorized, issued and outstanding following completion of the offering, see “11.2.1.3 Our Capital Stock Following Completion of the Global Offering.” Except as otherwise indicated, all information in this prospectus assumes: (i) the Preferred Stock Conversion will occur immediately prior to the completion of the global offering; (ii) the Convertible Notes Conversion will occur immediately prior to the completion of the global offering; (iii) the filing and effectiveness of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation in Delaware and the effectiveness of our amended and restated bylaws will each occur immediately prior to the completion of the global offering; (iv) the Class F Stock Issuance (as defined in “11.2.1.2 Initial Public Benefit Issuance, Preferred Stock Conversion, Convertible Notes Conversion and Class F Stock Issuance”) will occur immediately prior to the completion of the global offering; (v) the issuance of Class N common stock upon the closing of the concurrent private placement; (vi) no issuance of shares of Class E common stock prior to the completion of the global offering; (vii) no exercise of outstanding stock options or settlement of outstanding RSUs subsequent to September 30, 2026; and (viii) no exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of our Class A common stock from us in the global offering. 261 Holders of our Class A common stock are entitled to one vote for each share held on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T directors. Holders of our Class N common stock are not entitled to vote on any matter that is submitted to a vote of stockholders, except as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of the Class N common stock without so adversely affecting the Class A common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a series. The holder of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of the Class T common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class. Subject to preferences that may apply to any shares of preferred stock outstanding at the time, the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock are entitled to receive dividends out of funds legally available if our board of directors, in its discretion, determines to issue dividends and then only at the times and in the amounts that our board of directors may determine. Our Class T common stock and Class F common stock are not entitled to receive dividends. 11.2.1.1.2 Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock As of the date of this prospectus, the Company has issued the following redeemable convertible preferred stock. 262 The following table describes the key features of our redeemable convertible preferred stock as of the date of this prospectus, the general terms of which are set forth in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation: Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock Voting Non-voting Series A, C-1, D-1, D-2, E-1, F-1, G-1, and H-1 B, C-2, D-3, E-2, E-3, E-4, E-5, F-2, G-2, G-3, G-4, H-2, H-3, and H-4 Authorized number of shares(1) 439,710,597 600,730,055 Issued and outstanding number of shares(1) 438,406,253 414,987,790 Par value per share $0.00001 $0.00001 Votes per share The holders are entitled to the same voting rights and powers as the holders of the Class A common stock and to notice of any stockholders’ meeting in accordance with the bylaws of the Company, and the holders of Class A common stock and the holders of voting redeemable convertible preferred stock shall vote together as a single class on all matters. Each holder is entitled to the number of votes equal to the number of shares of Class A common stock into which such shares could be converted. The holders are not entitled to vote and shall have no voting rights, except as required by law or as specifically set forth in the certificate of incorporation, and shall have no right to vote in any election of the board of directors. Dividend rights The holders are entitled to receive, when and if declared by the Board, and prior and in preference to dividends on the Company’s common stock, dividends at the per annum rate of 6% of the applicable original issue price per share. Such dividends shall not be cumulative. After payment of such dividends, any additional dividends shall be distributed among the holders of common stock and redeemable convertible preferred stock in proportion to the number of shares of common stock that would be held by each such holder if all shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock were converted to common stock calculated on the record date for determination of holders entitled to such dividends. Redemption The holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock have no voluntary rights to redeem shares. The redeemable convertible preferred stockholders have liquidation preferences in the event of any liquidation transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event). Right to receive liquidation distributions In the event of any liquidation transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event), the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to receive, prior and in preference to any distribution of any of the assets of the Company to the holders of common stock, by reason of their ownership thereof, an amount per share equal to the original issue price for each outstanding share of redeemable convertible preferred stock then held (as adjusted for stock splits, stock dividends, reclassifications and the like), plus any declared but unpaid dividends on such shares. If, upon the occurrence of such event, the assets and funds thus distributed among the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be insufficient to permit the payment to such holders of the full aforesaid preferential amounts, then the entire assets and funds of the Company legally available for distribution shall be distributed ratably among the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock in proportion to the preferential amount each such holder is otherwise entitled to receive, and provided that the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock will be treated on an as-converted basis if, as a result of an actual conversion, such holder would receive, in the aggregate, an amount greater than the amount that would be distributed to such holder if such holder did not convert such series of preferred stock into shares of such series of common stock. Conversion rights and transferability In accordance with the terms as set forth in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation in effect as of the date of this prospectus, convertible into fully paid and non- assessable shares of Class A common stock. In accordance with the terms as set forth in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation in effect as of the date of this prospectus, convertible into fully paid and non-assessable shares of Class N common stock. Conversion ratio The conversion ratios for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock are 10:1, except for the Series D-1, Series D-2, and Series D-3, which are approximately 10.6:1, 10.4:1, and 10.6:1, respectively. Optional conversion Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into Class A common stock or Class N common stock, as applicable, at any time after the issuance of shares at the option of the holder. Automatic conversion Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall automatically convert to Class A common stock or Class N common stock, as applicable, at the applicable conversion ratio set forth above upon, among other things, the Company’s sale of its common stock in a firm commitment underwritten public offering pursuant to a registration statement under the U.S. Securities Act, resulting in at least
