and • no exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of our Class A common stock from us in the global offering. 11.2.1.3.1 Information on our Common Stock We have four classes of authorized common stock: • the class designated as Participating Common Stock, which is divided into two series: Class A common stock and Class N common stock; • Class T common stock, which is a special class of common stock that is issued to the LTBT; • Class F common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to the Founder LLC; and • Class E common stock, which is a special class of common stock that will be issued to our employees, excluding our co-founders. 11.2.1.3.1.1 Voting Rights • Class A common stock. Holders of our Class A common stock are entitled to one vote for each share held on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. Due to the voting power of our Class F common stock as described below, if the Founder LLC as holder of our single share of Class F common stock exercises its voting rights, the voting power of the holders of our Class A common stock will be limited to 49.9%. For information on the Founder LLC Agreement and the voting mechanics of our Class F common stock, see the sections titled “11.4 Founder LLC Agreement” and “11.5 Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.” • Class N common stock. Holders of our Class N common stock are not entitled to vote on any matter that is submitted to a vote of stockholders, except as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class N common stock without so adversely affecting our Class A common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a series. • Class T common stock. The holder of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors, the redemption of our Class E common stock,

 
269 certain amendments to the rights of our Class F common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class T common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holder to vote separately as a class. For additional information on the election and removal of directors, including the respective roles of the LTBT, the Founder LLC and the holders of our Class A common stock, see “4.1.1.2.1 Election and Removal of Directors” and “9.4 Board of Directors.” • Class F common stock. The Founder LLC as the holder of our single share of Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date on matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will be voted in the manner provided by the Founder LLC Agreement. See the section titled “11.5 Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.” • Class E common stock. The holders of our Class E common stock have no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with respect to the proposed nomination, removal or change in designation of the Specified Class T Director (in circumstances where our NGC does not concur with the LTBT’s proposed action), certain changes to the terms of the LTBT or the rights of our Class T common stock, the redemption of our Class T common stock, or as otherwise required by law, such as certain amendments to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that would adversely affect the powers, preferences, or special rights of our Class E common stock, on which the DGCL entitles such holders to vote separately as a class. 11.2.1.3.1.2 Conversion and Transferability • Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the section titled “8.6 Lock- Up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class A common stock can be transferred. • Class N common stock. The holders of our Class N common stock are primarily strategic business partners. Subject to compliance with applicable law and the restrictions described in the section titled “8.6 Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements,” our Class N common stock can be transferred. The shares of Class N common stock will automatically convert into an equal number of shares of Class A common stock upon a transfer effected through: (i) a registered offering or an open market sale of such shares or (ii) a transfer to a third party (A) that is not a holder of Class N common stock (or an affiliate of a holder of Class N common stock) and (B) that will not beneficially own or control more than 9.99% of the shares of any class or series of our equity securities after giving effect to the transfer. • Class T common stock. Our Class T common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Our Class T common stock is transferable only upon the approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. Because the persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold have the power to modify or terminate the LTBT and the rights of our Class T common stock entirely, there is no separate restriction on the identity of a permissible transferee of our Class T common stock. • Class F common stock. Our Class F common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock. Our Class F common stock is not transferable except in the case of a reorganization or redomiciliation of the Founder LLC that is approved by our board of directors and does not result in a change to the members of the Founder LLC. • Class E common stock. Our Class E common stock will not be convertible into any other class or series of capital stock and is not transferable. 11.2.1.3.1.3 Redemption • Class A common stock. Our Class A common stock will not be redeemable at our option or at the option of the holder. • Class N common stock. Our Class N common stock will not be redeemable at our option or at the option of the holder. • Class T common stock. Our Class T common stock will be redeemable for no consideration:

 
270 o if the Trustees are voting in favor of such redemption, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); o if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such redemption: o until the third anniversary of the completion of the global offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or o at any time, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 2⁄3% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or o if no Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such redemption, upon approval of 85% of the outstanding shares of Class A common stock. • Class F common stock. Our Class F common stock will be redeemable for no consideration (i) at the option of the Founder LLC, acting upon Supermajority approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, or (iii) upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, which will commence when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non- Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days. • Class E common stock. Our Class E common stock will not be redeemable at the option of the holder. Following an employee’s separation from employment with us other than for cause, one-half of such employee’s then- outstanding shares of Class E common stock will be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration annually, except that all shares of Class E common stock held by an employee will also be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration upon such employee’s death, incapacity, termination for cause, or commencement of service with a direct competitor. All shares of Class E common stock will also be automatically redeemed by us for no consideration (i) at such time as no Class F common stock remains outstanding, or (ii) upon the approval of (A) 80% of authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)), (B) the holder of our Class F common stock, and (C) the holder of our Class T common stock. 11.2.1.3.1.4 Dividend Rights Subject to preferences that may apply to any shares of preferred stock outstanding at the time, the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock are entitled to receive dividends out of funds legally available if our board of directors, in its discretion, determines to issue dividends and then only at the times and in the amounts that our board of directors may determine. Our Class T common stock, Class F common stock and Class E common stock are not entitled to receive dividends. See the section titled “12 Dividend Policy” for more information. 11.2.1.3.1.5 No Preemptive or Similar Rights Our common stock is not entitled to preemptive rights, and is not subject to redemption or sinking fund provisions (other than those providing for the redemption of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock for no consideration described above). 11.2.1.3.1.6 Right to Receive Liquidation Distributions If we become subject to a liquidation, dissolution, or winding up, including in bankruptcy, the assets legally available for distribution to our stockholders would be distributable ratably among the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock and any participating preferred stock outstanding at that time, subject to prior satisfaction of all outstanding debt and liabilities and the preferential rights of and the payment of liquidation preferences, if any, on any outstanding shares of our capital stock. In the event of our liquidation, dissolution, or winding up, including bankruptcy, holders of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock shall be entitled to receive par value ($0.00001) per share but shall not otherwise participate in such distributions.

 
271 11.2.1.3.2 Additional Information on Changes to the LTBT and Class T Common Stock The terms of the LTBT and the rights of the Class T common stock may be amended as follows: • if the Trustees are voting in favor of such amendments, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); • if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such amendments: o until the third anniversary of the completion of the global offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or o at any time, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or • if no Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of such amendments, upon approval of 85% of the outstanding Class A common stock. 11.2.1.3.3 Additional Information on Class N Common Stock Shares of our Class N common stock are not listed on a stock exchange and are not registered under the U.S. Securities Act. Shares of our Class N common stock will automatically convert into shares of Class A common stock upon a qualifying transfer, which shares would be subject to the resale restrictions and registration rights. Following the completion of the global offering and the concurrent private placement, shares of Class N common stock will consist of: • 4,183,660,974 shares, representing shares outstanding as of September 30, 2026, including shares to be issued immediately prior to the completion of the global offering pursuant to the Preferred Stock Conversion; • 846,840,960 shares issued in the Initial Public Benefit Issuance; • 276,827,518 shares to be issued immediately prior to the completion of the global offering in the Convertible Notes Conversion; • 1,563,617,444 shares issuable at certain intervals following the completion of the global offering pursuant to the conversion of any remaining outstanding convertible promissory notes at the applicable fixed conversion price that cannot be converted immediately prior to the completion of the global offering without exceeding such ownership cap; • the Matching Issuance; • 351,351,348 shares issuable immediately following the completion of the global offering pursuant to the concurrent private placement; and • shares issuable in connection with (i) the conversion of any convertible promissory notes that may be issued under our NPAs following the completion of the global offering, (ii) draws under our NPAs that are settled directly in shares of Class N common stock following the completion of the global offering, (iii) Public Benefit Issuances, (iv) donations that we match under our Donation Matching Plan, and (v) certain contractual rights to private placement following the completion of the global offering. For a description of the conversion mechanics of the outstanding notes and the rights to future issuances of notes and Class N common stock, see the section titled “5.12.3 Convertible Notes.” Additionally, certain holders of our Class N common stock are entitled to registration rights with respect to their shares, the exercise of which could facilitate sales of large blocks of our shares into the public market following any applicable lock-up period. See the section titled “11.2.5 Registration Rights” for a description of these registration rights.

 
272 11.2.1.3.4 Sunset Provisions Class T Sunset Time Class F Sunset Time Trigger The Class T Sunset Time occurs when no Class T common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class T common stock or an amendment to the rights of our Class T common stock that eliminates our Class T common stock, which in each case requires the approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. The Trust Amendment Threshold may be satisfied as follows: • if the Trustees are voting in favor of the action, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); • if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of the action: o until the third anniversary of the completion of the global offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or o at any time, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or The Class F Sunset Time occurs on the earlier of (i) the time when no Class F common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class F common stock agreed to by a Supermajority of the Continuing Founders or upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, and (ii) the completion of the Class F Transition Period. The Class F Transition Period commences when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days. A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co- founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of the global offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause,” which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of the global offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co- founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence. • if no Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of the action, upon approval of 85% of the outstanding Class A common stock. The Class T Sunset Time does not occur automatically upon the lapse of time or the occurrence of specific events. Any action resulting in the occurrence of the Class T Sunset Time requires approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. The Class T Sunset Time, once triggered, is not subject to extension, delay, or waiver. Removals due to resignation, death, or the occurrence of the tenth anniversary of the completion of the global offering occur automatically without any determination by any other person. Removals due to incapacity require determination by a qualified physician jointly selected by the affected Continuing Founder and a majority of the other Continuing Founders (in the case of physical or mental impairment) or determination by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders (in the case of wrongful imprisonment, unlawful detention, or captivity or restraint), subject to the affected Continuing Founder’s right to contest such determination. Removals due to cause require an affirmative determination by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, subject to the affected Continuing Founder’s right to contest such determination or, in the case of specified categories of cause, to cure the basis for such removal.

 
273 Class T Sunset Time Class F Sunset Time Removals due to incapacity, cause, or the failure to maintain the minimum ownership threshold require prior written notice from the Founder LLC by action of a majority of the other Continuing Founders. If a Continuing Founder is removed due to death or incapacity during the first ten years following the completion of the global offering, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC and will count toward the three Continuing Founders required to avoid triggering the Class F Transition Period until the tenth anniversary of the completion of the global offering. The Class F Sunset Time, once triggered, is not subject to extension, delay, or waiver. Changes in Voting Power and Director Election and Removal Rights Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the LTBT, as the sole holder of Class T common stock, will generally have the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. The share of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, including with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors or as required by law. Following the Class T Sunset Time, if our Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, will elect all of our directors. Because our Class F common stock is entitled to an aggregate number of votes equal to 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock, the Founder LLC would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. If neither our Class T common stock nor Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date and, together with our Class A common stock, voting together as a single class, will elect our directors other than the Class T directors and decide all other matters put to a vote of stockholders generally. Immediately after the Class F Sunset Time, if our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the LTBT would continue to have the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who would constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. However, the LTBT would no longer need to comply with the procedures for nomination, removal, or change in the Class T director designated as the Specified Class T Director. In such a case, our Class A common stock would elect and remove the remaining directors and decide all other matters put to a vote of stockholders generally. If neither our Class T common stock nor Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. 11.2.1.3.5 Preferred Stock After the completion of the global offering, no shares of our preferred stock will be outstanding. Pursuant to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, our board of directors (if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve) will have the authority, subject to limitations set forth in such amended and restated certificate of incorporation or prescribed by Delaware law, to issue preferred stock in one or more series, to establish from time to time the number of shares to be included in each series and to fix the designation, powers, preferences, and rights of the shares of each series and any of its qualifications, limitations, or restrictions, in each case without further vote or action by our stockholders; provided that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors shall not designate or issue any series of preferred stock without the affirmative vote or consent of the Founder LLC. Our board of directors (if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve) can also increase or decrease the number of shares of any series of preferred stock, but not below the number of shares of that series then outstanding, without any further vote or action by our stockholders. Subject to limitations set forth in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, or prescribed by Delaware law, we may authorize the issuance of preferred stock with voting or conversion rights that could adversely affect the voting power or other rights of the holders of our common stock, including the likelihood that such

 
274 holders will receive dividend payments and payments upon liquidation. If we were to issue shares of preferred stock with the right to vote on matters submitted to our stockholders generally, the voting power of our outstanding Class A common stock would be diluted, while the voting power of our Class F common stock would remain fixed at an aggregate of 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to such matters. The issuance of preferred stock, while providing flexibility in connection with possible acquisitions and other corporate purposes, could, among other things, have the effect of delaying, deferring, or preventing a change in control of our company and might adversely affect the market price of our Class A common stock and the voting and other rights of the holders of our Class A common stock. We have no current plan to issue any shares of preferred stock. 11.2.2 Convertible Securities For information on the Company’s convertible securities, see the section titled “5.12.3 Convertible Notes” and Note 9 and Note 10 to our consolidated financial statements, which are incorporated in, and form part of, this prospectus (see “10.1 Consolidated Financial Statements”), as well as “11.2.1.2 Initial Public Benefit Issuance, Preferred Stock Conversion, Convertible Notes Conversion and Class F Stock Issuance” with respect to the Preferred Stock Conversion and the Convertible Notes Conversion. 11.2.3 Options As of September 30, 2026, we had outstanding options to purchase an aggregate of 1,774,342,693 shares of our Class A common stock, with a weighted-average exercise price of $2.91 per share, under our 2021 Plan. For information regarding the terms of the Company’s outstanding options, see the section titled “9.12.2.18 Equity Plans.” 11.2.4 RSUs As of September 30, 2026, we had outstanding 1,127,993,950 shares of our Class A common stock issuable upon the vesting and settlement of RSUs under our 2021 Plan. For information regarding the terms of the Company’s outstanding RSUs, see the section titled “9.12.2.18 Equity Plans.” 11.2.5 Registration Rights After the completion of the global offering, certain holders of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to rights with respect to the registration of their shares under the U.S. Securities Act. These registration rights are contained in our IRA. We and certain holders of our stock are parties to our IRA. In addition, we are party to separate registration rights agreements with each of Google and Broadcom (the “Infrastructure Partner RRA”) that we entered into in connection with NPAs with those parties, which provide Google and Broadcom with registration rights separate from the registration rights under our IRA, as described below under “11.2.5.4 Registration Rights of Google” and “11.2.5.5 Registration Rights of Broadcom.” The registration rights set forth in our IRA will expire upon the earliest to occur of (i) the second anniversary of the date of completion of the global offering, (ii) with respect to any particular holder, when such stockholder is able to sell all of its shares pursuant to Rule 144 under the U.S. Securities Act or any similar exemption during any three-month period, or (iii) the termination of our IRA. We will pay the registration expenses (other than underwriting discounts and commissions) of the holders of the shares registered pursuant to the registrations described below. In an underwritten offering, the managing underwriter, if any, has the right, subject to specified conditions, to limit the number of shares such holders may include. The registration rights described in this section do not entitle any holder to notice of, or to include shares in, the global offering. The exercise of these registration rights is subject to the lock-up agreements described in the section titled “8.6 Lock-Up and Market Standoff Agreements;” to the extent applicable to the shares being registered. The shares of Class N common stock to be sold in the concurrent private placement are not subject to those lock-up agreements. 11.2.5.1 Demand Registration Rights After the completion of the global offering and the closing of the concurrent private placement, the holders of up to 8,527,685,412 shares of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to certain demand registration rights, including those set forth in our IRA and Google’s registration rights described below under “11.2.5.4 Registration Rights of Google.” Under our IRA, at any time beginning six months after the effective date of the global offering, the holders of at least 60% of the shares registrable under our IRA that are entitled to vote can request that we register the offer and sale of their shares. Such a request for registration must cover securities, the anticipated aggregate offering price of which, net of underwriting discounts and commissions, is at least $200,000,000. We are obligated to effect only two such registrations. If we determine that it would be seriously detrimental to us and our stockholders to effect such a demand registration, we have the right to defer such registration, not more than twice in any 12-month period, for a period of up to 120 days. Additionally, we will

 
275 not be required to effect a demand registration during the period beginning 90 days prior to our good faith estimate of the date of filing of, and ending on a date 90 days following the effective date of, a registration statement relating to an offering by us (or, in the case of the global offering, ending on a date 180 days following the effective date of such related registration statement), provided that we are actively employing in good faith all reasonable efforts to cause such registration statement to become effective. We are also not obligated to effect a demand registration if the initiating holders propose to dispose of shares that may be immediately registered on Form S-3 pursuant to the Form S-3 registration rights described below. 11.2.5.2 Piggyback Registration Rights After the completion of the global offering, if we propose to register the offer and sale of our Class A common stock (including shares issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) under the U.S. Securities Act, in connection with the public offering of such Class A common stock the holders of up to 10,066,010,871 shares of our Class A common stock will be entitled to certain “piggyback” registration rights allowing the holders to include their shares in such registration, subject to certain marketing and other limitations and the registration rights under our convertible note agreements, which consist of the Google RRA and the Infrastructure Partner RRA described below. As a result, whenever we propose to file a registration statement under the U.S. Securities Act, other than with respect to (i) a registration related to any employee benefit plan or a corporate reorganization or other transaction covered by Rule 145 promulgated under the U.S. Securities Act, (ii) a registration on any registration form that does not include substantially the same information as would be required to be included in a registration statement covering the sale of the shares, or (iii) a registration in which the only Class A common stock being registered is Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of debt securities that are also being registered, the holders of these shares are entitled to notice of the registration and have the right, subject to certain limitations and/or cutbacks, to include their shares in the registration. If the underwriters limit the number of shares to be included in an underwritten offering, the number of registrable shares included may not be reduced below 20% of the total securities included in the offering, and shares held by our co- founders may not be included if any registrable shares held by other selling holders are excluded. 11.2.5.3 S-3 Registration Rights After the completion of the global offering and the closing of the concurrent private placement, the holders of up to 8,527,685,412 shares of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to certain Form S-3 registration rights, including those set forth in our IRA and Google’s registration rights described below under “11.2.5.4 Registration Rights of Google.” Under our IRA, the holders of at least 60% of the shares registrable under our IRA that are entitled to vote may make a written request that we register the offer and sale of their shares on a registration statement on Form S-3 if we are eligible to file a registration statement on Form S-3 so long as the request covers securities the anticipated aggregate public offering price of which is at least $2,000,000, net of any underwriting discounts and commissions. These stockholders may make an unlimited number of requests for registration on Form S-3; however, we will not be required to effect a registration on Form S-3 if we have effected two such registrations within the 12-month period preceding the date of the request. Additionally, if we determine that it would be seriously detrimental to us and our stockholders to effect such a registration, we have the right to defer such registration, not more than once in any 12-month period, for a period of up to 120 days. We are also not required to effect a registration on Form S-3 during the period ending 180 days after the effective date of a registration statement subject to the piggyback registration rights described above. 11.2.5.4 Registration Rights of Google We entered into the Google RRA in May 2026 in connection with our Google 2026 NPA, pursuant to which Google may acquire shares of our capital stock. Under the Google RRA, shares of our capital stock held by Google that are not covered by the registration rights under our IRA are registrable, subject to customary exceptions. During the one-year period following the effective date of the registration statement with respect to the U.S. offering, Google may make a single demand that we register the resale of all of its registrable shares that are not then salable pursuant to Rule 144. In addition, once we are eligible to use Form S-3, we are required to register on Form S-3, within 60 days of each quarterly closing under the Google 2026 NPA, the resale of the registrable shares acquired at such closing and of any registrable shares not previously registered, and to keep such registrations effective for so long as Google holds registrable shares. Except as described below regarding a Restricted Period Demand, registrations under the Google RRA are subject to customary deferral and blackout provisions, including our right, if our board of directors determines in good faith that filing a demand registration statement would be seriously detrimental to us and our stockholders, to defer the filing until the earlier of 10 business days after we file our next Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q and 120 days after we receive the demand (the “deferral right”). Google may not exercise its registration rights under the Google RRA after

 
276 February 7, 2033 or, if earlier, the date that is 12 months following the final quarterly closing under the Google 2026 NPA. In connection with the concurrent private placement, we entered into a Class N common stock purchase agreement with Google (the “Google Purchase Agreement”), under which shares of our Class A common stock underlying shares of Class N common stock that Google purchases in the concurrent private placement will be registrable under the Google RRA. The Google Purchase Agreement also amends the Google RRA such that, until the earlier of the second trading day following our release of earnings for the quarter ending March 31, 2027 and the 180th day after the date of this prospectus (the “Restricted Period”), we are not required to publicly file a registration statement under the Google RRA. If Google makes its demand during the Restricted Period (a “Restricted Period Demand”), we must use our reasonable best efforts to confidentially submit a registration statement within 60 days after receiving the demand, publicly file it no later than the later of two business days after the Restricted Period ends and the date on which it would otherwise be required to be filed after giving effect to the deferral right, and cause it to become effective as promptly as practicable thereafter. Other than the deferral right, we may not exercise any suspension, deferral, or blackout right in a manner that would reasonably be expected to delay the filing or effectiveness of that registration statement. 11.2.5.5 Registration Rights of Broadcom We entered into the Infrastructure Partner RRA in June 2026 in connection with the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA that may be assigned by Broadcom, subject to our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), to a designated financial partner, pursuant to which we may issue convertible promissory notes to Broadcom or a designated financial partner. If we grant registration rights to other securityholders, or amend their existing registration rights, on terms more favorable than those provided to the holder of these registrable shares, we must offer to amend the rights of the holder of these registrable shares to be at least as favorable, and the holder of these registrable shares is entitled to proportionate treatment if lock-up or similar restrictions are waived for other stockholders in connection with a registration, in each case subject to specified exceptions. The Infrastructure Partner RRA terminates upon the earlier of the date on which the holder of these registrable shares and its permitted transferees no longer hold registrable shares and the date that is nine months after the latest maturity date of any outstanding note issued under the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA. The sales of these securities were made without any general solicitation or advertising. 11.3 Anti-Takeover Provisions Certain provisions of Delaware law, our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering that are summarized below, may have the effect of delaying, deferring, or discouraging another person from acquiring control of us. They are also designed, in part, to encourage persons seeking to acquire control of us to negotiate first with our board of directors. We believe that the benefits of increased protection of our potential ability to negotiate with an unsolicited acquirer outweigh the disadvantages of discouraging a proposal to acquire us because negotiation of these proposals could result in an improvement of their terms. 11.3.1 Delaware Law We have elected not to be governed by the provisions of Section 203 of the DGCL prior to the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, but our amended and restated certificate of incorporation will provide that the restrictions contained in Section 203 will apply to us immediately following the later to occur of either the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time. Following the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, we will thereafter be governed by Section 203, which generally prohibits a public Delaware corporation from engaging in a “business combination” with an “interested stockholder” for a period of three years after the date of the transaction in which the person became an interested stockholder, unless: • the business combination or transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder was approved by the board of directors prior to the time that the stockholder became an interested stockholder; • upon consummation of the transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder, the interested stockholder owned at least 85% in voting power of the voting stock of the corporation outstanding at the time the transaction commenced, excluding shares owned by directors who are also officers of the corporation and shares owned by employee stock plans in which employee participants do not have the right to determine confidentially whether shares held subject to the plan will be tendered in a tender or exchange offer; or • at or subsequent to the time the stockholder became an interested stockholder, the business combination was approved by the board of directors and authorized at an annual or special meeting of the stockholders, and not by written consent, by the affirmative vote of at least two-thirds of the outstanding voting stock which is not owned by the interested stockholder. In general, Section 203 defines a “business combination” to include mergers, asset sales, and other transactions resulting in financial benefit to a stockholder and an “interested stockholder” as a person who, together with affiliates and associates, owns, or is an affiliate or associate of the corporation and within three years did own, 15% or more in voting power of the corporation’s outstanding voting stock.

 
279 11.3.2 Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws Provisions Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, will include a number of provisions that could deter hostile takeovers or delay or prevent changes in control of our board of directors or management team, including but not limited to the following: 11.3.2.1 Multi-Class Common Stock As described above in the sections titled “11.2.1.3 Our Capital Stock Following Completion of the Global Offering” and “9.4 Board of Directors,” our amended and restated certificate of incorporation provides for a multi-class common stock structure. Under this governance structure, we expect that the LTBT and the Founder LLC will collectively have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors, and the Founder LLC will have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future, including the approval by our stockholders of significant corporate transactions such as a merger or other sale of the Company or its assets. Such transactions also require approval of our board of directors, a majority of whom are elected by the LTBT. Holders of our Class A common stock generally will not be able to affect the outcome of any matter submitted to a vote of our stockholders or the election of our directors, regardless of how they vote, unless a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted (in which case our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter). 11.3.2.2 Classified Board Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering will provide that, prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next annual meeting and until the election and qualification of their successor, or their earlier death, resignation, or removal. Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time, our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires. As a result, only one class of directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual meeting of stockholders following their election and until their successor has been elected and qualified, or until their earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of one-third of our directors. 11.3.2.3 Board Vacancies Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that (i) prior to the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of our Class T common stock can fill vacant directorships of any Class T director, subject to the nomination procedures for the Specified Class T Director; and (ii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors can be filled by (A) our board of directors, in accordance with, and following receipt of written notice from, the Founder LLC recommending the person proposed to fill such director seat or (B) the holders of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together or acting by written consent. Following the Class F Sunset Time, only our board of directors will be permitted to fill vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors. Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set only with the approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); provided that until the earlier to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, such total number of authorized directors must be an odd number. Following the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set with the approval of a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. These provisions would prevent a stockholder from increasing the size of our board of directors and then gaining control of our board of directors by filling the resulting vacancies with its own nominees. This will make it more difficult to change the composition of our board of directors.

 
280 11.3.2.4 Advance Notice Requirements for Stockholder Proposals and Director Nominations Our amended and restated bylaws will provide advance notice procedures for stockholders, other than holders of Class T common stock or Class F common stock nominating directors in accordance with nomination procedures in our certificate of incorporation or the Stockholders’ Agreement, seeking to bring business before our annual meeting of stockholders or to nominate candidates for election as directors at a meeting of stockholders. Our amended and restated bylaws will also specify certain requirements regarding the form and content of a stockholder’s notice. These provisions might preclude our stockholders from bringing matters before our annual meeting of stockholders or from making nominations for directors at a meeting of stockholders if the proper procedures are not followed. In addition, our NGC will have the right to receive 30 days’ prior written notice of any nomination of persons to serve as a director by the LTBT or the Founder LLC or the proposed removal of such directors, as well as appointments and removals of the Trustees. Our NGC may waive such notice periods in its discretion. We expect that these provisions may also discourage or deter a potential acquirer from conducting a solicitation of proxies to elect the acquirer’s own slate of directors or otherwise attempting to obtain control of the Company. 11.3.2.5 Special Meetings of Stockholders Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that special meetings of stockholders may be called only by (i) our board of directors acting pursuant to a resolution adopted by a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors; (ii) the chairperson of our board of directors; (iii) our Chief Executive Officer; (iv) our President; (v) following the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the directors who are not Class T directors; (vi) prior to the Class F Sunset Time and only with respect to a special meeting at which holders of our Class E common stock will be asked to vote on a proposal, the secretary of the Company; or (vii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC as the holder of our Class F common stock. 11.3.2.6 No Cumulative Voting The DGCL provides that stockholders are not entitled to cumulate votes in the election of directors unless a corporation’s certificate of incorporation provides otherwise. Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation does not provide for cumulative voting. 11.3.2.7 Action by Written Consent Prior to the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, stockholders may act by written consent only with respect to (i) any action to nominate, elect, or remove directors or appoint a director to fill any vacancy or newly created directorship; (ii) any action to satisfy certain redemption and protective provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation related to our Class F common stock, Class T common stock, and Class E common stock; and (iii) any matter on which stockholders vote together as a single class if such matter is first approved or requested by our board of directors. From and after the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of the single share of Class F common stock may act by written consent, and from and after the Class F Sunset Time, only the holder of the single share of Class T common stock may act by written consent, in each case, only with respect to the actions described above. From and after the occurrence of both the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, any action required or permitted to be taken by the stockholders must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any action required or permitted to be taken by the holders of Class E common stock must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders. 11.3.2.8 Amendment of Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws Provisions Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the voting power of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws. Following the Class F Sunset Time, 66 2/3% of the voting power of our Class A common stock can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws. 11.3.2.9 Issuance of Undesignated Preferred Stock Subject to limitations in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, or prescribed by Delaware law, our board of directors will have the authority, if 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) approve, and without further action by our stockholders, to issue up to 30,000,000,000 shares of undesignated preferred stock with rights and preferences, including voting rights, designated from time to time by our board of directors, provided that, prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors shall not designate

 
281 or issue any series of preferred stock without the affirmative vote or consent of the Founder LLC. The existence of authorized but unissued shares of preferred stock would enable our board of directors to render more difficult or to discourage an attempt to obtain control of us by means of a merger, tender offer, proxy contest, or other means. 11.3.2.10 Exclusive Forum Our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, will provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware does not have jurisdiction, another State court in Delaware or the federal district court for the District of Delaware) will, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for (i) any derivative action or proceeding brought on our behalf, (ii) any action asserting a claim of breach of a fiduciary duty owed by any of our current or former directors, stockholders, or officers or other employees to us or our stockholders, (iii) any action arising pursuant to any provision of the DGCL or as to which the DGCL confers jurisdiction upon the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, (iv) any action arising pursuant to or to interpret, apply, enforce, or determine the validity of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation or our amended and restated bylaws, or (v) any action asserting a claim governed by the internal affairs doctrine, except for, in all cases, any claim as to which such court determines that there is an indispensable party not subject to the jurisdiction of such court (and the indispensable party does not consent to the personal jurisdiction of such court within 10 days following such determination). Section 22 of the U.S. Securities Act establishes concurrent jurisdiction for federal and state courts over U.S. Securities Act claims. Accordingly, both state and federal courts have jurisdiction to hear such claims. To prevent having to litigate claims in multiple jurisdictions and the threat of inconsistent or contrary rulings by different courts, among other considerations, our amended and restated bylaws will also provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United States will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for resolving any complaint asserting a cause or causes of action arising under the U.S. Securities Act against any person in connection with any offering of our securities, including, without limitation, any auditor, underwriter, expert, control person, or other defendant. Unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the United States District Court for the District of Delaware will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for the resolution of any derivative action or proceeding brought to enforce any duty or liability created by the U.S. Exchange Act or the rules or regulations thereunder. All other claims arising under the U.S. Exchange Act may be brought in any federal court of competent jurisdiction. Any person or entity purchasing, holding, or otherwise acquiring any interest in our securities shall be deemed to have notice of and consented to these provisions. We note that stockholders cannot waive compliance (or consent to non-compliance) with the federal securities laws and the rules and regulations thereunder. 11.4 Founder LLC Agreement Our co-founders intend to enter into the Founder LLC Agreement. We expect the Founder LLC Agreement to become effective substantially concurrently with the filing and acceptance of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. Our Class F common stock will be held by the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock will be voted by the Founder LLC in a manner determined pursuant to the Founder LLC Agreement. Generally, the Founder LLC will vote as determined by a majority of the Continuing Founders. Our seven co-founders will each initially be a Continuing Founder. Upon the incapacity or death of any of our co-founders, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC as a Continuing Founder until the tenth anniversary of the completion of the global offering. When there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non- Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days, the 450-day Class F Transition Period will commence. Upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, all of our Class F common stock and Class E common stock then issued and outstanding will be redeemed by us for no consideration and certain other governance changes will take effect. Regardless of the length of time that has elapsed since the completion of the global offering or the circumstances that resulted in the removal of a Continuing Founder, one or more successor members may be admitted to the Founder LLC during the Class F Transition Period, as needed to ensure that there are three Continuing Founders serving until completion of the Class F Transition Period. The admission of any successor member during the Class F Transition Period will not cure the event that commenced the Class F Transition Period or extend the Class F Transition Period.

 
282 A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co- founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of the global offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause” (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of the global offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence. Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. If a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted, then our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). With respect to certain matters, our Class F common stock will be voted “for” the proposal only if a greater threshold of Continuing Founders agree, and if the greater threshold is not met, our Class F common stock will be voted “against” the proposal. See the section titled “11.5 Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.” The Founder LLC Agreement will not govern the voting of any shares of our Class A common stock held by the co- founders or their related holders. Each co-founder (or their related holders) will be able to vote shares of our Class A common stock held by them in their discretion, regardless of the manner in which the Founder LLC will vote our Class F common stock. For additional information on the election and removal of directors, including the respective roles of the LTBT, the Founder LLC and the holders of our Class A common stock, see “9.4 Board of Directors.” 11.5 Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics Under the terms of the Founder LLC Agreement, the manner in which our Class F common stock will be voted will be determined as follows: Matter Threshold(1) If threshold is met Otherwise General stockholder matters Majority(2) Class F common stock is voted accordingly. Class F common stock is voted proportionately with the votes of Class A common stock cast (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). Amendments to Class F rights Supermajority(3)(4) Class F common stock is voted “for” the proposal. Class F common stock is voted “against” (or “withhold” as to) the proposal. Amendments to LTBT / Class T rights Trust Amendment Supermajority(4)(5) Class F common stock is voted “for” the proposal. Class F common stock is voted “against” (or “withhold” as to) the proposal. Written consent The applicable majority, Supermajority(3), or Trust Amendment Supermajority(5) if action were taken at a meeting. Consent is delivered with respect to our Class F common stock. No consent is delivered with respect to our Class F common stock. ______________ (1) Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. (2) If a majority of the Continuing Founders deliver the same instruction as to how the votes corresponding to our Class F common stock shall be cast, including “for,” “against,” or “withhold,” but excluding an instruction to “abstain,” our Class F common stock will be voted accordingly. If a majority of the Continuing Founders deliver instructions to “abstain” or do not deliver the same or any instructions, our Class F common stock will be voted proportionately with the votes of Class A common stock cast (subject to a quorum of a majority of the outstanding Class A common stock). For example, if a quorum is present and 75% of the votes cast by the Class A common stock entitled to vote were cast “for” and 25% of the votes cast by the Class A common stock entitled to vote were cast “against,” the Class F common stock would cast its votes proportionally, with 75% voted “for” and 25% voted “against,” such that the votes cast by the holders of Class A common stock determine the outcome of the matter.

 
283 (3) “Supermajority” means the total number of Continuing Founders entitled to vote, minus one, delivers instructions to vote “for” the proposal. If there are fewer than three Continuing Founders, a Supermajority requires unanimity of Continuing Founders. (4) If a proposal requires both a Supermajority and a Trust Amendment Supermajority, both thresholds must be satisfied. (5) A “Trust Amendment Supermajority” will be satisfied if (i) 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders, rounded up to the nearest whole number, deliver instructions to vote “for” the proposal, and approval by 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock) and a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of the outstanding shares of Class A common stock) is also obtained or (ii) until the third anniversary of the completion of the global offering, the Continuing Founders unanimously deliver instructions to vote “for” the proposal, and approval by a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock) and a majority of the votes cast by our outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding shares of Class A common stock) is also obtained.
